recipes.search: gajar matar sabzi (carrot & peas stir-fry) gajar matar sabzi (carrot & peas stir-fry) chef magic – sauté auto 14 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegan • everyday • low-oil ingredients 3 medium carrots, diced 1 cup green peas (fresh or frozen) 1 tsp cumin seeds (jeera) 1/4 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1/2 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 1 tbsp oil salt to taste chopped coriander (dhania) to garnish method 1 add oil and cumin seeds to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) until the seeds splutter. 2 add the diced carrots, turmeric and chilli powder; sauté for 6 minutes. 3 add the peas and salt, with a splash of water; continue on sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) for 6 minutes until the carrots are tender and the peas are cooked through. 4 garnish with coriander and serve as a simple side with dal-rice or roti. tip: a five-minute, everyday sabzi that barely needs watching — good for busy weeknights.

recipes.title: Aloo Paratha (Stuffed Potato Flatbread)
recipes.search: aloo paratha (stuffed potato flatbread) aloo paratha (stuffed potato flatbread) chef magic (knead & filling) → airfryer (cook) 200°c knead 5 min + cook 8 min makes 4 vegetarian • everyday prep ahead: rest the dough for 15 minutes before rolling so it’s easier to shape. ingredients 2 cups whole wheat flour water as needed 1/2 tsp salt (for dough) 2 medium potatoes, boiled and mashed 1 green chilli (hari mirch), finely chopped 1 tsp ginger (adrak), grated 1/2 tsp roasted cumin powder (bhuna jeera powder) 1/4 tsp garam masala 2 tbsp chopped coriander (dhania) salt to taste (for filling) oil or ghee, for cooking method 1 preheat: when you reach the airfryer step, preheat it to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 in chef magic, add flour, salt (for dough) and a little water; select knead (speed 2–3, no heat), adding water gradually until a soft dough forms. rest 15 minutes. 3 mix mashed potato with green chilli, ginger, cumin powder, garam masala, coriander and salt for the filling. 4 divide dough into 4 balls; flatten each, place a portion of filling in the centre, and seal into a ball. roll out gently into a flatbread, dusting with flour as needed. 5 brush both sides lightly with oil and place in the airfryer basket. 6 cook at 200°c for 8 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden-brown spots appear on both sides. 7 serve hot with curd, pickle or butter. tip: roll gently and evenly — pressing too hard can push the filling through the dough.

recipes.title: Moong Dal Cheela (Savoury Lentil Pancake)
recipes.search: moong dal cheela (savoury lentil pancake) moong dal cheela (savoury lentil pancake) airfryer – fry (griddle-style) 190°c 12 min makes ~6 gluten-free • vegan • high-protein • everyday prep ahead: soak the moong dal for at least 3 hours (or overnight) before grinding into a batter. ingredients 1 cup yellow moong dal, soaked 3+ hours 1 green chilli (hari mirch) 1/2 inch ginger (adrak) 1/4 tsp cumin seeds (jeera) salt to taste water as needed 1/4 cup finely chopped onion & coriander (optional) oil for cooking method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 190°c for 4 minutes before adding the food to the basket. 2 drain the soaked dal and blend with green chilli, ginger, cumin seeds, salt and just enough water into a smooth, pourable batter. 3 stir in chopped onion and coriander if using. 4 brush the airfryer’s baking pan or a flat oven-safe dish with oil and preheat. 5 pour a thin layer of batter, spray the top lightly with oil, and cook at 190°c for 6 minutes per side until golden and firm. 6 repeat with the remaining batter; serve hot with chutney or curd. tip: a protein-rich, everyday breakfast alternative to besan chilla — no fermentation or resting needed beyond the soak.

recipes.title: Pyaz Tamatar ki Sabzi (Onion-Tomato Sabzi)
recipes.search: pyaz tamatar ki sabzi (onion-tomato sabzi) pyaz tamatar ki sabzi (onion-tomato sabzi) chef magic – sauté auto 16 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegan • everyday • low-oil ingredients 3 onions, sliced 3 tomatoes, chopped 1 tsp cumin seeds (jeera) 1/4 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1/2 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 1/2 tsp coriander powder (dhania powder) 1 tbsp oil salt to taste chopped coriander (dhania) to garnish method 1 add oil and cumin seeds to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) until the seeds splutter. 2 add the sliced onions and cook for 7 minutes until soft and lightly golden. 3 add tomatoes, turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder; continue on sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) for 7 minutes until the tomatoes fully break down. 4 season with salt and garnish with coriander; serve with roti or dal-rice. tip: one of the simplest everyday sabzis — barely needs a shopping list beyond onions and tomatoes.

recipes.title: Dahi Bhindi (Okra in Yogurt Gravy)
recipes.search: dahi bhindi (okra in yogurt gravy) dahi bhindi (okra in yogurt gravy) chef magic – sauté auto 20 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegetarian • everyday prep ahead: wash and dry the okra completely before slicing, and whisk the yogurt smooth before it goes in. ingredients 300g okra (bhindi), sliced 1 cup yogurt, whisked smooth 1 onion, finely chopped 1 tsp cumin seeds (jeera) 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1/2 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 1 tsp coriander powder (dhania powder) 2 tbsp oil salt to taste chopped coriander (dhania) to garnish method 1 add 1 tbsp oil to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook the okra for 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned and no longer sticky; remove and set aside. 2 add the remaining oil and cumin seeds; sauté until they splutter, then add onion and cook 5 minutes until soft. 3 add turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder; sauté 1 minute. 4 lower to sauté (speed 1–2, ~100–110°c), stir in the whisked yogurt and salt, and simmer gently for 4 minutes, stirring often. 5 fold the cooked okra back in and warm through for 2 minutes. garnish with coriander. tip: pre-cooking the okra separately before adding the yogurt is what keeps it from turning slimy in this dish.

recipes.title: Punjabi Chole (Chickpea Curry)
recipes.search: punjabi chole (chickpea curry) punjabi chole (chickpea curry) chef magic – sauté + boil auto 32 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegan • high-protein • everyday prep ahead: soak dried chickpeas overnight, or use 2 cans of drained, rinsed chickpeas to save time. ingredients 2 cups chickpeas, soaked overnight 2 onions, chopped 2 tomatoes, pureed 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 2 tsp chole masala 1/2 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 2 tbsp oil 1 tea bag (for colour, optional) salt to taste coriander (dhania) to garnish method 1 add soaked chickpeas, water, salt and the tea bag (if using) to the jar; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and cook until fully tender. discard the tea bag. 2 add oil to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook onions until golden. 3 add ginger-garlic paste, tomato puree, chole masala and chilli powder; sauté until the oil separates. 4 stir the cooked chickpeas back in with a little of their cooking water; simmer on sauté (speed 1–2, ~100–110°c) for 9 minutes until thick. garnish with coriander.

recipes.title: Rajma Masala (Kidney Bean Curry)
recipes.search: rajma masala (kidney bean curry) rajma masala (kidney bean curry) chef magic – sauté + boil auto 32 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegan • high-protein • everyday prep ahead: soak rajma (kidney beans) overnight for best texture and shorter cooking time. ingredients 2 cups rajma (kidney beans), soaked overnight 2 onions, chopped 2 tomatoes, pureed 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1.5 tsp rajma/garam masala 1/2 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 2 tbsp oil salt to taste coriander (dhania) to garnish method 1 add soaked rajma, water and salt to the jar; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and cook until soft and creamy inside. 2 add oil to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook onions until golden. 3 add ginger-garlic paste, tomato puree, masala and chilli powder; sauté until the oil separates. 4 stir the cooked rajma back in with a little of its cooking water; simmer on sauté (speed 1–2, ~100–110°c) for 10 minutes, mashing a few beans against the side to thicken. garnish with coriander.

recipes.title: Palak Paneer
recipes.search: palak paneer palak paneer chef magic – boil + whisk + sauté auto 21 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegetarian • high-protein • everyday ingredients 250g spinach, washed 200g paneer, cubed 1 onion, chopped 1 tomato, chopped 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1/2 tsp garam masala 2 tbsp cream 1 tbsp butter 1 green chilli (hari mirch) salt to taste method 1 add spinach and a splash of water to the jar; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) for 2 minutes just until wilted. select whisk/blend (speed 8–10) with the green chilli to puree; set aside. 2 add butter to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook onion until golden, then add ginger-garlic paste and tomato, cooking until soft. 3 add garam masala and the spinach puree; simmer on sauté (speed 1–2, ~100–110°c) for 5 minutes. 4 gently fold in paneer cubes and cream; sauté 2 minutes just to warm through.

recipes.title: Baingan Bharta (Smoky Roasted Eggplant Mash)
recipes.search: baingan bharta (smoky roasted eggplant mash) baingan bharta (smoky roasted eggplant mash) airfryer or chef magic — pick whichever you have free — roast 22 min + cook 14 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegan • everyday ingredients 1 large eggplant (brinjal) 1 onion, chopped 1 tomato, chopped 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1/2 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 2 tbsp oil 1 green chilli (hari mirch), chopped salt to taste coriander (dhania) to garnish method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 airfryer: prick the eggplant a few times with a fork, place in the basket, and roast at 200°c for 22 minutes, turning halfway, until the skin is charred and the flesh is soft. cool slightly, peel off the charred skin, and mash the flesh. 3 chef magic: add oil to the jar, select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c), and cook onions until golden. 4 add ginger-garlic paste, tomato, green chilli, turmeric and chilli powder; sauté until the oil separates. 5 fold in the mashed roasted eggplant and salt; sauté for 9 minutes until well combined. garnish with coriander. tip: the charred skin is where the smokiness comes from — don’t skip the roasting step even if you’re short on time.

recipes.title: Gujarati Dhokla
recipes.search: gujarati dhokla gujarati dhokla chef magic – steam auto batter rest 15 min + steam 16 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegetarian • low-oil • everyday prep ahead: let the batter rest 15 minutes after adding fruit salt (eno) or baking soda so it can aerate properly. ingredients 1.5 cups besan (gram flour (besan)) 1 tbsp semolina (sooji) 1 tbsp curd 1 tbsp oil 1 tsp ginger (adrak)-green chilli (hari mirch) paste 1 tsp sugar 3/4 cup water 1 tsp fruit salt (eno) or baking soda salt to taste 1 tsp mustard seeds (rai) & curry leaves (kadi patta) for tempering method 1 whisk besan, semolina, curd, oil, ginger-chilli paste, sugar, salt and water into a smooth, lump-free batter. 2 just before steaming, stir in the fruit salt or baking soda; the batter will turn frothy. pour immediately into a greased dish that fits the steamer tray. 3 add water to the jar and fit the steamer tray; select steam (100°c steam, paddle off) and cook for 16 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. 4 temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves in a little hot oil, and pour over the dhokla before cutting into pieces.

recipes.title: Sambar
recipes.search: sambar sambar chef magic – boil + sauté auto 28 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegan • high-fibre • everyday ingredients 1 cup toor dal, washed 1 cup mixed vegetables (drumstick, carrot, pumpkin), chopped 2 tbsp sambar powder 1 tsp tamarind (imli) paste 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1 tsp mustard seeds (rai) 9 curry leaves (kadi patta) 1 dried red chilli (lal mirch) 1 tbsp oil 3 cups water salt to taste method 1 add dal, vegetables, turmeric and water to the jar; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and cook until dal and vegetables are fully soft. 2 stir in sambar powder, tamarind paste and salt; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) again for 5 minutes to blend the flavours. 3 temper mustard seeds, curry leaves and dried red chilli in oil, then stir into the sambar.

recipes.title: Rasam
recipes.search: rasam rasam chef magic – boil auto 16 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegan • gut-friendly • everyday ingredients 2 tomatoes, chopped 1 tbsp tamarind (imli) paste 1 tbsp rasam powder 1/4 tsp turmeric (haldi) 2 cups water 1 tsp mustard seeds (rai) 9 curry leaves (kadi patta) 1 tsp cumin seeds (jeera) 1 tsp ghee salt to taste coriander (dhania) to garnish method 1 add tomatoes, tamarind paste, rasam powder, turmeric, water and salt to the jar; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and cook for 11 minutes until fragrant. 2 add ghee, mustard seeds, cumin seeds and curry leaves directly in; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) for 2 minutes to temper. 3 garnish with coriander and serve hot.

recipes.title: Vegetable Upma
recipes.search: vegetable upma vegetable upma chef magic – sauté + boil auto 16 min — serves 3 vegetarian • everyday • low-oil ingredients 1 cup semolina (sooji) 1/2 cup mixed vegetables (carrot, peas, beans), chopped 1 onion, chopped 1 tsp mustard seeds (rai) 9 curry leaves (kadi patta) 1 tbsp oil 2 cups water salt to taste lemon juice to finish method 1 add oil, mustard seeds and curry leaves to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) until seeds splutter. 2 add onion and vegetables; sauté 4 minutes. 3 add semolina and roast 2 minutes, stirring, until lightly toasted. 4 add water and salt; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and cook, stirring, until the water is absorbed and the mixture turns fluffy. finish with lemon juice.

recipes.title: Kadai Paneer
recipes.search: kadai paneer kadai paneer chef magic – sauté + boil auto 21 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegetarian • high-protein • everyday ingredients 200g paneer, cubed 1 capsicum, cubed 2 onions, chopped 2 tomatoes, pureed 1 tbsp coarsely crushed coriander seeds (sookha dhania) & dried red chilli (kadai masala) 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 2 tbsp oil 1/2 tsp garam masala salt to taste method 1 add oil to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook onions until golden. 2 add ginger-garlic paste and crushed kadai masala; sauté 2 minutes until fragrant. 3 add tomato puree and salt; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) briefly, then return to sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook until the oil separates. 4 add capsicum and paneer; sauté gently for 4 minutes, then sprinkle garam masala before serving.

recipes.title: Pav Bhaji
recipes.search: pav bhaji pav bhaji chef magic – boil + sauté auto 32 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegetarian • everyday ingredients 2 potatoes, chopped 1 cup cauliflower florets 1/2 cup peas 1 capsicum, chopped 2 tomatoes, chopped 1 onion, chopped 2 tbsp pav bhaji masala 1/2 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 3 tbsp butter salt to taste pav (bread rolls) & chopped onion, lemon, to serve method 1 add potatoes, cauliflower, peas and enough water to the jar; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and cook until fully soft. 2 add butter to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook onion until golden, then add capsicum and tomatoes, cooking until mushy. 3 add pav bhaji masala and chilli powder; sauté 2 minutes. 4 add the boiled vegetables with a little of their water; mash roughly and simmer on sauté (speed 1–2, ~100–110°c) for 5 minutes until thick. serve with buttered, toasted pav.

recipes.title: Malai Kofta
recipes.search: malai kofta malai kofta airfryer or chef magic — pick whichever you have free — fry koftas 16 min (airfryer) or 11 min (chef magic); gravy 20 min in chef magic — serves 4 vegetarian • everyday ingredients 2 potatoes, boiled & mashed 150g paneer, grated 2 tbsp cornflour salt to taste 2 tomatoes 10 cashews 1 onion 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1/2 tsp garam masala 2 tbsp cream 1 tbsp butter oil (for frying koftas) method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 190°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 mix mashed potato, grated paneer, cornflour and salt; shape into small balls. 3 option a – airfryer: spray generously with oil, arrange in the basket, air-fry at 190°c for 16 minutes, turning once, until golden and firm. 4 option b – chef magic: add oil to the jar, select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c), and shallow-fry the koftas, turning gently, for 11 minutes until golden on all sides. remove and set aside. 5 make the gravy in chef magic (butter, onion, tomato, cashews, ginger-garlic — sauté, blend smooth, then simmer with cream and garam masala for 15 minutes) and pour hot over the koftas just before serving so they stay crisp longer.

recipes.title: Vegetable Biryani
recipes.search: vegetable biryani vegetable biryani airfryer or chef magic — pick whichever you have free — prep 15 min + cook 28 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegetarian • everyday prep ahead: soak basmati rice for 20 minutes before cooking for the fluffiest, most separate grains. ingredients 1.5 cups basmati rice, soaked 20 min 2 cups mixed vegetables, chopped 1 onion, sliced 1/2 cup yogurt 1 tbsp biryani masala 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 2 tbsp ghee a few saffron (kesar) strands in warm milk 2.5 cups water or stock salt to taste fried onions & coriander (dhania) to garnish method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 180°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 par-cook vegetables with yogurt, biryani masala and ginger-garlic paste using chef magic’s sauté for 9 minutes. 3 option a – airfryer (layered): layer the par-cooked vegetables and soaked rice in an oven-safe dish, pour over hot water/stock, drizzle with saffron milk and ghee, cover tightly with foil, and bake at 180°c for 28 minutes until rice is fluffy; rest covered for 5 minutes before fluffing and garnishing. 4 option b – chef magic (one-pot): add ghee to the jar, select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook onions until golden, then add vegetables, yogurt, biryani masala and ginger-garlic paste, cooking 9 minutes; add soaked rice, water/stock, saffron milk and salt; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and cook until the water is absorbed and rice is fluffy, about 16 minutes; rest 5 minutes, then fluff and garnish with fried onions and coriander.

recipes.title: Karela Fry (Bitter Gourd Fry)
recipes.search: karela fry (bitter gourd fry) karela fry (bitter gourd fry) airfryer or chef magic — pick whichever you have free — 22 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegan • bengali prep ahead: salt sliced karela and rest 18 minutes, then squeeze out the bitter liquid before cooking. ingredients 3 karela (bitter gourd), thinly sliced 1 tsp salt (for resting) 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1/2 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 1 tbsp mustard oil (or any oil) salt to taste (for cooking) method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 190°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 option a – airfryer: squeeze salted karela dry, toss with oil, turmeric and chilli powder, spread in a single layer in the basket, and air-fry at 190°c for 16 minutes, shaking every 5 minutes, until deep brown and crisp. 3 option b – chef magic: add oil to the jar, select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c), add squeezed karela, turmeric and chilli powder, and cook, stirring occasionally, for 16 minutes until deep brown and crisp, uncovered so moisture escapes. tip: salting and squeezing out the liquid is what cuts the bitterness — don’t skip this step.

recipes.title: Shukto (Bengali Mixed Vegetable Stew)
recipes.search: shukto (bengali mixed vegetable stew) shukto (bengali mixed vegetable stew) chef magic – sauté + boil auto 28 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegetarian • bengali • gut-friendly ingredients 2 cups mixed vegetables (drumstick, potato, brinjal, bitter gourd, raw banana), chopped 1 tbsp mustard-poppy seed paste (or plain mustard paste (sarson paste)) 1/2 tsp panch phoron (bengali five-spice) 1 cup milk 1 tsp ghee 1 tbsp mustard oil (sarson ka tel) salt & sugar to taste method 1 add mustard oil and panch phoron to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) until fragrant. 2 add the vegetables and sauté 4 minutes. 3 add the mustard-poppy paste, milk, salt and a pinch of sugar; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and cook until vegetables are tender and the gravy thickens slightly. 4 finish with a drizzle of ghee before serving. tip: shukto is traditionally eaten first with rice at the start of a bengali meal — it’s meant to be mild and slightly bitter.

recipes.title: Aloo Posto (Potatoes in Poppy Seed Paste)
recipes.search: aloo posto (potatoes in poppy seed paste) aloo posto (potatoes in poppy seed paste) chef magic – sauté + boil auto 21 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegan • bengali prep ahead: soak poppy seeds (posto) in warm water for 25 minutes before grinding to a smooth paste. ingredients 3 medium potatoes, diced 3 tbsp poppy seeds (posto), soaked and ground to a paste 1 tsp kalonji (nigella seeds) 2 green chillies (hari mirch), slit 2 tbsp mustard oil (sarson ka tel) 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) salt to taste method 1 add mustard oil and kalonji to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) for 1 minute until fragrant. 2 add potatoes and turmeric; sauté 5 minutes until lightly coated and starting to soften. 3 add the poppy seed paste, green chillies, salt and a little water; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and cook until potatoes are fully tender and the paste thickens around them. tip: posto paste can stick if rushed — keep the heat gentle and stir occasionally for the smoothest texture.

recipes.title: Jhinge Aloo Bata Sorshe Diye (Ridge Gourd & Potato in Mustard Paste)
recipes.search: jhinge aloo bata sorshe diye (ridge gourd & potato in mustard paste) jhinge aloo bata sorshe diye (ridge gourd & potato in mustard paste) chef magic – sauté + boil auto 19 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegan • bengali prep ahead: soak mustard seeds in warm water for 18 minutes before grinding into a paste, with a green chilli, for a smoother, ingredients 2 ridge gourds (jhinge), peeled and chopped 1 potato, diced 2 tbsp mustard seeds (rai), soaked and ground to a paste 1/2 tsp nigella seeds (kalonji) 1 green chilli (hari mirch), slit 2 tbsp mustard oil (sarson ka tel) 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) salt to taste method 1 add mustard oil and nigella seeds to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) for 1 minute. 2 add potato and turmeric; sauté 4 minutes. 3 add ridge gourd and sauté a further 4 minutes until it starts to soften and release water. 4 stir in the mustard paste, green chilli and salt; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and cook until vegetables are fully tender and the gravy is thickened.

recipes.title: Begun Bhaja (Crispy Fried Eggplant Slices)
recipes.search: begun bhaja (crispy fried eggplant slices) begun bhaja (crispy fried eggplant slices) airfryer or chef magic — pick whichever you have free — 16 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegan • bengali prep ahead: salt eggplant slices and rest 10 minutes to draw out excess moisture, then pat dry. ingredients 1 large eggplant (brinjal), sliced into rounds 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1/2 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) salt to taste 2 tbsp mustard oil (or rice flour for extra crispness) method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 190°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 option a – airfryer: toss eggplant slices with turmeric, chilli powder, salt and oil (coat lightly in rice flour if using), arrange in a single layer in the basket, and air-fry at 190°c for 14 minutes, flipping halfway, until deep golden and crisp at the edges. 3 option b – chef magic: add oil to the jar, select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c), add coated eggplant slices, and cook, turning occasionally, for 11 minutes until golden-brown on both sides.

recipes.title: Cholar Dal (Bengal Gram Dal with Coconut)
recipes.search: cholar dal (bengal gram dal with coconut) cholar dal (bengal gram dal with coconut) chef magic – sauté + boil auto 32 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegetarian • bengali • high-protein prep ahead: soak chana dal (bengal gram) for at least 1 hour to shorten the cooking time. ingredients 1 cup chana dal, soaked 1 hour 2.5 cups water 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 2 tbsp grated coconut 1 tbsp raisins 1 bay leaf (tej patta) 1 tsp cumin seeds (jeera) 1 dried red chilli (lal mirch) 1 tbsp ghee 1 tsp sugar salt to taste method 1 add dal, water, turmeric and salt to the jar; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and cook until dal is soft but grains hold their shape. 2 add ghee, cumin seeds, bay leaf and dried red chilli directly to the cooked dal; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) for 2 minutes to temper. 3 stir in coconut, raisins and sugar; sauté a further 2 minutes until fragrant.

recipes.title: Chorchori (Mixed Vegetable Dry Curry)
recipes.search: chorchori (mixed vegetable dry curry) chorchori (mixed vegetable dry curry) chef magic – sauté auto 21 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegan • bengali • everyday ingredients 2.5 cups mixed vegetables (pumpkin, potato, brinjal, beans), chopped 1/2 tsp panch phoron 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1 green chilli (hari mirch), slit 1 tbsp mustard oil (sarson ka tel) salt to taste method 1 add mustard oil and panch phoron to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) until fragrant. 2 add all vegetables, turmeric, green chilli and salt. 3 continue on sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) for 19 minutes, stirring occasionally, until vegetables are tender and slightly mashed at the edges.

recipes.title: Aloo Bhate (Bengali-Style Mashed Potato)
recipes.search: aloo bhate (bengali-style mashed potato) aloo bhate (bengali-style mashed potato) chef magic – boil then mix auto 15 min — serves 2 gluten-free • vegan • bengali • no-cook finish • everyday ingredients 3 medium potatoes 1 tbsp mustard oil (sarson ka tel) 1 small onion, finely chopped 1 green chilli (hari mirch), finely chopped salt to taste chopped coriander (dhania) method 1 add whole potatoes with enough water to cover them to the jar; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and cook until fork-tender. 2 peel and roughly mash the potatoes by hand in a bowl. 3 mix in mustard oil, onion, green chilli, salt and coriander while still warm.

recipes.title: Chhanar Dalna (Bengali Paneer & Potato Curry)
recipes.search: chhanar dalna (bengali paneer & potato curry) chhanar dalna (bengali paneer & potato curry) chef magic – sauté + boil auto 26 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegetarian • bengali • high-protein ingredients 250g paneer, cubed 2 potatoes, cubed 1 tsp cumin seeds (jeera) 1 bay leaf (tej patta) 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1 tsp cumin (jeera)-coriander powder (dhania powder) 1/2 tsp garam masala 2 tbsp mustard oil (sarson ka tel) salt & sugar to taste chopped coriander (dhania) to garnish method 1 add mustard oil to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and lightly fry the paneer cubes for 3 minutes until golden; remove and set aside. 2 add cumin seeds and bay leaf to the same jar; sauté until fragrant, then add potatoes and turmeric; sauté 5 minutes. 3 add cumin-coriander powder, salt, a pinch of sugar and a little water; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and cook until potatoes are tender. 4 return the paneer to the jar with garam masala; simmer on sauté (speed 1–2, ~100–110°c) for 3 minutes. garnish with coriander. tip: a pinch of sugar is traditional in bengali paneer curries — it rounds out the mustard oil’s sharpness.

recipes.title: Lauki Aloo Curry (Bottle Gourd & Potato Curry)
recipes.search: lauki aloo curry (bottle gourd & potato curry) lauki aloo curry (bottle gourd & potato curry) chef magic – sauté + boil auto 22 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegan • everyday • low-oil ingredients 1 lauki (bottle gourd), peeled and cubed 2 medium potatoes, cubed 1 tsp cumin seeds (jeera) 1 tomato, chopped 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1/2 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 1/2 tsp coriander powder (dhania powder) 1 tbsp oil salt to taste chopped coriander (dhania) to garnish method 1 add oil and cumin seeds to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) until the seeds splutter. 2 add the potatoes and sauté for 4 minutes. 3 add the tomato, turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder; sauté 3 minutes until the tomato softens. 4 add the lauki and salt, with a splash of water; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and cook for 12 minutes until the lauki and potatoes are fully tender. 5 mash a few pieces lightly against the side of the jar to thicken the gravy slightly. garnish with coriander. tip: lauki releases a lot of its own water as it cooks — add only a splash of water at the start, or the curry ends up thin.

recipes.title: Aloo Arbi Gravy (Potato & Colocasia Curry)
recipes.search: aloo arbi gravy (potato & colocasia curry) aloo arbi gravy (potato & colocasia curry) chef magic – sauté + boil auto 24 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegan • everyday • north indian prep ahead: pat the boiled arbi completely dry and peel it while still warm — a wet or cold arbi turns slimy and won't take on colour. ingredients 250g arbi (colocasia/taro root), boiled, peeled and halved 2 medium potatoes, cubed 1 onion, finely chopped 2 tomatoes, chopped 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1 tsp cumin seeds (jeera) 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 1 tsp coriander powder (dhania powder) 1/2 tsp garam masala 1/2 tsp amchur (dry mango powder) 2 tbsp oil salt to taste chopped coriander (dhania) to garnish method 1 add oil and cumin seeds to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) until the seeds splutter. 2 add the onion and sauté for 5 minutes until golden. 3 add ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder; sauté 2 minutes until fragrant. 4 add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until soft and the oil separates at the edges. 5 add the potatoes and arbi with a splash of water; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and cook for 10 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the arbi is coated in a thick gravy. 6 stir in garam masala and amchur; cook 2 minutes more. garnish with coriander and serve hot with roti. tip: don't stir too vigorously once the arbi goes in — it breaks down easily and can make the gravy gluey rather than glossy.

recipes.title: Sheem er Paturi (Flat Beans Steamed in Mustard)
recipes.search: sheem er paturi (flat beans steamed in mustard) sheem er paturi (flat beans steamed in mustard) chef magic – steam auto prep 15 min + steam 18 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegan • bengali prep ahead: soak mustard seeds in warm water for 20 minutes before grinding, with a green chilli, for a smoother, less bitter ingredients 300g sheem (flat/hyacinth beans), thinly sliced 2 tbsp mustard seeds (rai), soaked and ground to a paste 2 tbsp grated coconut 2 green chillies (hari mirch), slit (plus 1 for the paste) 3 tbsp mustard oil (sarson ka tel) 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) salt & sugar to taste banana leaf or foil, to wrap method 1 toss the sliced sheem with the mustard-coconut paste, turmeric, mustard oil, a pinch of sugar and salt until well coated. 2 spoon the mixture onto a piece of banana leaf or foil, top with slit green chillies, and fold into a sealed parcel. 3 add water to chef magic’s jar and fit the steamer tray; place the parcel on top. 4 select steam (100°c steam, paddle off) and cook for 18 minutes until the sheem is tender and the parcel is fragrant. 5 rest for 2 minutes, then unwrap and serve hot with steamed rice. tip: paturi is traditionally wrapped in banana leaf, which adds its own aroma during steaming — foil works fine, but banana leaf

recipes.title: Tandoori Soya Chaap
recipes.search: tandoori soya chaap tandoori soya chaap airfryer – grill 200°c 17 min — serves 4 high-protein • vegetarian • everyday prep ahead: marinate the soya chaap for at least 1 hour (or overnight in the fridge) for the best flavour. ingredients 500g soya chaap (stick or boneless), cut into pieces 1/2 cup thick yogurt 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1.5 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 1 tsp garam masala 1 tsp kasuri methi (dried fenugreek (methi)), crushed 1 tbsp mustard oil (sarson ka tel) salt to taste 1 tbsp lemon juice method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food to the basket. 2 whisk together yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chilli powder, garam masala, crushed kasuri methi, mustard oil, salt and lemon juice. 3 add the soya chaap pieces to the marinade, coat well, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour. 4 skewer or arrange the marinated chaap pieces in a single layer in the basket. 5 grill at 200°c for 17 minutes, turning once halfway, until charred at the edges. 6 serve hot with onion rings and mint chutney.

recipes.title: Achari Soya Chaap (Pickle-Spiced)
recipes.search: achari soya chaap (pickle-spiced) achari soya chaap (pickle-spiced) chef magic – sauté auto 21 min — serves 4 high-protein • vegetarian • everyday ingredients 500g soya chaap, cut into pieces 1 tsp mustard seeds (rai) 1 tsp fennel seeds (saunf) 1/2 tsp fenugreek (methi) seeds 1/2 tsp nigella (kalonji) seeds 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1.5 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 1 onion, chopped 2 tbsp oil 1 tbsp lemon juice salt to taste method 1 add oil to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and add mustard seeds, fennel seeds, fenugreek seeds and nigella seeds; cook 1 minute until fragrant. 2 add the chopped onion and cook for 4 minutes until golden. 3 add turmeric, chilli powder and the soya chaap pieces; sauté for 13 minutes, stirring occasionally, until well coated and lightly browned. 4 finish with lemon juice and salt to taste; toss well before serving.

recipes.title: Malai Soya Chaap (Creamy)
recipes.search: malai soya chaap (creamy) malai soya chaap (creamy) chef magic – sauté auto 24 min — serves 4 high-protein • vegetarian • everyday ingredients 500g soya chaap, cut into pieces 1 onion, pureed 10 cashews, soaked and ground to a paste 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1/2 cup fresh cream 1 tsp garam masala 2 tbsp butter 1 green chilli (hari mirch), chopped salt to taste method 1 add butter to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook the onion puree for 6 minutes until the raw smell disappears. 2 add ginger-garlic paste and the ground cashew paste; cook for 4 minutes. 3 add the soya chaap pieces and chopped green chilli; sauté for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. 4 stir in cream, garam masala and salt; simmer on sauté (speed 1–2, ~100–110°c) for 4 minutes until the gravy thickens.

recipes.title: Soya Chaap Tikka Masala
recipes.search: soya chaap tikka masala soya chaap tikka masala airfryer (grill the tikka) → chef magic (make the 200°c grill 15 min + gravy 16 min gravy) — serves 4 high-protein • vegetarian • everyday prep ahead: marinate the soya chaap pieces for at least 30 minutes before grilling. ingredients 500g soya chaap, cut into pieces 1/2 cup yogurt 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1.5 tsp tikka masala 2 onions, chopped 2 tomatoes, pureed 1 tbsp butter 1/2 cup cream 1 tsp garam masala salt to taste method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 mix the soya chaap with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste and tikka masala; marinate for at least 30 minutes. 3 arrange the marinated chaap in a single layer in the airfryer basket. 4 grill at 200°c for 15 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges. 5 in chef magic, add butter; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook onions until golden, then add tomatoes and cook until the oil separates, about 9 minutes. 6 add the grilled chaap, cream and garam masala; simmer on sauté (speed 1–2, ~100–110°c) for 5 minutes and serve hot.

recipes.title: Soya Chunks (Nutrela) Curry
recipes.search: soya chunks (nutrela) curry soya chunks (nutrela) curry chef magic – boil + sauté auto 26 min — serves 4 gluten-free • high-protein • vegetarian • everyday prep ahead: soak dried soya chunks in hot water for 15 minutes, then squeeze out the water before cooking. ingredients 1.5 cups dried soya chunks 2 onions, chopped 2 tomatoes, pureed 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1.5 tsp curry powder or garam masala 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 2 tbsp oil 1 cup water salt to taste coriander (dhania) to garnish method 1 soak soya chunks in hot water for 15 minutes; squeeze out excess water thoroughly. 2 add oil to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook onions for 6 minutes until golden. 3 add ginger-garlic paste, tomatoes, turmeric and curry powder; sauté for 7 minutes until the oil separates. 4 add the soaked soya chunks, water and salt; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and cook for 9 minutes until the gravy thickens. garnish with coriander.

recipes.title: Soya Keema (Minced Soya Curry)
recipes.search: soya keema (minced soya curry) soya keema (minced soya curry) chef magic – sauté auto 19 min — serves 4 gluten-free • high-protein • vegan • everyday prep ahead: soak soya granules (keema) in hot water for 10 minutes, then drain and squeeze dry. ingredients 1.5 cups soya granules (keema) 1 onion, finely chopped 1 tomato, finely chopped 1/2 cup peas 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1 tsp garam masala 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 2 tbsp oil salt to taste coriander (dhania) to garnish method 1 soak soya granules in hot water for 10 minutes; drain and squeeze out excess water. 2 add oil to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook onion for 4 minutes until golden. 3 add ginger-garlic paste, tomato, turmeric and garam masala; sauté for 6 minutes. 4 add the soaked soya granules and peas; sauté for 9 minutes, stirring occasionally, until dry and well combined. garnish with coriander.

recipes.title: Amritsari Chole Kulche (Chole Only)
recipes.search: amritsari chole kulche (chole only) amritsari chole kulche (chole only) chef magic – boil + sauté auto 38 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegan • high-protein • everyday prep ahead: soak dried chickpeas overnight in plenty of water. ingredients 2 cups chickpeas, soaked overnight 2 tbsp amritsari chole masala 2 onions, chopped 2 tomatoes, pureed 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1 black tea bag 2 tbsp oil salt to taste 1 tbsp lemon juice chopped onion, ginger (adrak) juliennes and coriander (dhania) to garnish method 1 add soaked chickpeas, enough water to cover, the tea bag and salt to the jar; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and cook for 22 minutes until soft and darker in colour. discard the tea bag. 2 add oil to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook onions for 6 minutes until deep golden. 3 add ginger-garlic paste, tomatoes and chole masala; sauté for 9 minutes until the oil separates. 4 add the boiled chickpeas with a little cooking liquid; simmer on sauté (speed 1–2, ~100–110°c) for 9 minutes until thick. finish with lemon juice and garnish with onion, ginger and coriander.

recipes.title: Matar Paneer
recipes.search: matar paneer matar paneer chef magic – sauté auto 21 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegetarian • high-protein • everyday ingredients 200g paneer, cubed 1 cup green peas 1 onion, chopped 2 tomatoes, pureed 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1 tsp garam masala 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 2 tbsp oil salt to taste coriander (dhania) to garnish method 1 add oil to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook onion for 4 minutes until golden. 2 add ginger-garlic paste, tomatoes, turmeric and garam masala; sauté for 7 minutes until the oil separates. 3 add peas and a splash of water; simmer on sauté (speed 1–2, ~100–110°c) for 6 minutes until peas are tender. 4 gently fold in the paneer cubes and salt; sauté for 2 minutes just to warm through. garnish with coriander.

recipes.title: Vegetable Manchurian (Dry)
recipes.search: vegetable manchurian (dry) vegetable manchurian (dry) airfryer (fry the balls) → chef magic (toss in 200°c fry 15 min + toss 9 min sauce) — serves 4 vegan • everyday ingredients 2 cups finely shredded cabbage, carrot & capsicum 3 tbsp cornflour 2 tbsp maida (plain flour) 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste), divided salt to taste oil spray 1 onion, chopped 2 tbsp soy sauce 1 tbsp vinegar 1 tbsp chilli sauce 1/2 cup water mixed with 1 tsp cornflour method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 mix shredded vegetables with cornflour, maida, half the ginger-garlic paste and salt; shape into small balls. 3 spray the balls generously with oil and arrange in the airfryer basket. 4 air-fry at 200°c for 15 minutes, shaking halfway, until golden and crisp. 5 in chef magic, add a little oil; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook the chopped onion with the remaining ginger-garlic paste for 2 minutes. 6 add soy sauce, vinegar, chilli sauce and the cornflour-water mix; cook 2 minutes until it thickens slightly, then toss in the fried balls just before serving so they stay crisp.

recipes.title: Paneer Do Pyaza
recipes.search: paneer do pyaza paneer do pyaza chef magic – sauté auto 24 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegetarian • high-protein • everyday ingredients 250g paneer, cubed 3 onions — 2 cubed into petals, 1 finely chopped 2 tomatoes, pureed 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1 tsp cumin seeds (jeera) 1 tsp coriander powder (dhania powder) 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 1/2 tsp garam masala 2 tbsp oil salt to taste chopped coriander (dhania) to garnish method 1 add oil and cumin seeds to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) until fragrant. 2 add the finely chopped onion and cook for 6 minutes until golden. 3 add ginger-garlic paste, tomato puree, turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder; sauté for 7 minutes until the oil separates. 4 add the onion petals and a splash of water; simmer on sauté (speed 1–2, ~100–110°c) for 5 minutes until the petals soften but still hold their shape. 5 gently fold in the paneer cubes, garam masala and salt; sauté for 3 minutes just to warm through. garnish with coriander. tip: keep the onion petals separated rather than fully mixed in — do pyaza means ‘double onion’ and the petals should stay

recipes.title: Paneer Pasanda
recipes.search: paneer pasanda paneer pasanda chef magic – sauté auto 26 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegetarian • high-protein • mughlai prep ahead: slice the paneer into thin, flat pieces rather than cubes — this is what gives pasanda its signature look. ingredients 300g paneer, cut into thin flat slices 2 tbsp chopped nuts & raisins, for the stuffing (optional) 1 onion, roughly chopped 12 cashews, soaked 1 tomato, chopped 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1/2 tsp garam masala 1/4 tsp white pepper (safed mirch) 3 tbsp cream 2 tbsp ghee 1 tsp sugar salt to taste method 1 if stuffing, sandwich a little chopped nuts and raisins between two thin paneer slices; set aside. 2 add ghee to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft. 3 add soaked cashews, tomato and ginger-garlic paste; cook for 6 minutes, then select whisk/blend (speed 8–10) to purée smooth. 4 return to sauté (speed 1–2, ~100–110°c); add garam masala, white pepper, sugar and salt, and simmer for 6 minutes. 5 gently slide in the paneer slices and cream; sauté 5 minutes just to warm through, spooning gravy over the top instead of stirring hard so the slices stay intact. tip: handle the paneer slices gently once they’re in the gravy — pasanda pieces are meant to stay whole, not break up like a

recipes.title: Paneer Lababdar
recipes.search: paneer lababdar paneer lababdar chef magic – sauté auto 24 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegetarian • high-protein • everyday ingredients 250g paneer, cubed 2 onions, roughly chopped 3 tomatoes, chopped 12 cashews, soaked 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1 tsp kashmiri chilli powder (mirch powder) 1/2 tsp garam masala 1 tsp kasuri methi (dried fenugreek (methi)), crushed 3 tbsp cream 1 tbsp butter 1 tsp sugar salt to taste method 1 add butter to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook the onions for 6 minutes until soft. 2 add tomatoes, cashews and ginger-garlic paste; cook for 8 minutes until the tomatoes break down completely. 3 select whisk/blend (speed 8–10) to purée the mixture smooth, then return it to the jar. 4 select sauté (speed 1–2, ~100–110°c); stir in chilli powder, garam masala, sugar and salt, and simmer for 4 minutes. 5 add the paneer cubes, cream and crushed kasuri methi; sauté gently for 4 minutes until the gravy turns rich and glossy. tip: lababdar should be thicker and richer than a standard makhani gravy — resist adding water; let the cashews and cream

recipes.title: Paneer Jalfrezi
recipes.search: paneer jalfrezi paneer jalfrezi chef magic – sauté auto 20 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegetarian • high-protein • everyday ingredients 250g paneer, cut into batons 1 onion, sliced 1 capsicum, julienned 1 tomato, sliced 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1 tsp cumin seeds (jeera) 1 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1 tsp coriander powder (dhania powder) 1 tbsp tomato ketchup or paste 1 tbsp soy sauce (optional, for a restaurant-style edge) 2 tbsp oil salt to taste method 1 add oil and cumin seeds to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) until they splutter. 2 add onion and cook for 4 minutes until just softened but still with some bite. 3 add ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, chilli powder and coriander powder; sauté 2 minutes. 4 add capsicum and tomato; sauté for 5 minutes, keeping the vegetables crisp-tender rather than fully soft. 5 stir in ketchup, soy sauce if using, and salt; fold in the paneer batons and sauté gently for 4 minutes until just warmed through. tip: jalfrezi is meant to be quick and high-heat, keeping the vegetables crunchy — don’t let it simmer down into a soft gravy.

recipes.title: Paneer Korma
recipes.search: paneer korma paneer korma chef magic – sauté auto 24 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegetarian • high-protein • mughlai ingredients 250g paneer, cubed 1 onion, roughly chopped 1/4 cup cashews, soaked 2 tbsp yogurt, whisked 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1/2 tsp garam masala 1/4 tsp white pepper (safed mirch) 2 green cardamom (elaichi), 1 cinnamon stick (dalchini) 2 tbsp ghee 1/2 cup warm milk salt to taste fried onions & coriander (dhania) to garnish method 1 add ghee, cardamom and cinnamon to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) for 1 minute until fragrant. 2 add the onion and cook for 6 minutes until soft and lightly golden. 3 add cashews and ginger-garlic paste; cook 4 minutes, then select whisk/blend (speed 8–10) with a splash of milk to purée smooth. 4 return to sauté (speed 1–2, ~100–110°c); whisk in the yogurt off the direct heat edge, then stir in garam masala, white pepper and salt, simmering for 5 minutes. 5 add the paneer and remaining warm milk; sauté gently for 4 minutes until the gravy is pale, rich and creamy. garnish with fried onions and coriander. tip: add yogurt only once the pan has come off high heat, stirring constantly — this is what stops a korma gravy from splitting.

recipes.title: Achari Paneer (Pickle-Spiced)
recipes.search: achari paneer (pickle-spiced) achari paneer (pickle-spiced) chef magic – sauté auto 20 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegetarian • high-protein • everyday ingredients 250g paneer, cubed 1 tsp mustard seeds (rai) 1 tsp fennel seeds (saunf) 1/2 tsp fenugreek (methi) seeds 1/2 tsp nigella (kalonji) seeds 1 onion, chopped 1 tomato, chopped 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1.5 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 2 tbsp mustard oil (sarson ka tel) 1 tbsp yogurt 1 tbsp lemon juice salt to taste method 1 add mustard oil to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and add mustard, fennel, fenugreek and nigella seeds; cook 1 minute until fragrant. 2 add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until golden. 3 add tomato, turmeric and chilli powder; sauté 6 minutes until the tomato breaks down and the oil separates. 4 whisk in the yogurt and salt; simmer on sauté (speed 1–2, ~100–110°c) for 3 minutes. 5 gently fold in the paneer cubes; sauté for 4 minutes until well coated, then finish with lemon juice. tip: toast the whole spices just until they smell fragrant — a few seconds too long and the fenugreek turns bitter.

recipes.title: Hariyali Paneer Tikka (Green Herb Marinade)
recipes.search: hariyali paneer tikka (green herb marinade) hariyali paneer tikka (green herb marinade) airfryer – grill 200°c 13 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegetarian • high-protein • everyday prep ahead: marinate the paneer and vegetables for at least 30 minutes, up to 2 hours in the fridge, for the best flavour. ingredients 400g paneer, cubed 1/2 cup thick yogurt 1 cup mint & coriander leaves (hara dhania) 2 green chillies (hari mirch) 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1 tsp garam masala 1 tbsp mustard oil (sarson ka tel) bell peppers & onion, cubed salt to taste lemon wedges to serve method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food to the basket. 2 blend mint, coriander and green chillies with a splash of water into a smooth paste. 3 whisk the green paste into the yogurt with ginger-garlic paste, garam masala, mustard oil and salt. 4 marinate the paneer and vegetables in this mix for at least 30 minutes. 5 skewer or arrange in the basket; grill at 200°c for 13 minutes, turning once, until lightly charred at the edges. 6 serve with lemon wedges and extra mint chutney.

recipes.title: Amritsari Paneer Tikka
recipes.search: amritsari paneer tikka amritsari paneer tikka chef magic (marinade) → airfryer (grill) 200°c marinate 30 min + grill 14 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegetarian • high-protein • punjabi prep ahead: marinate the paneer for at least 30 minutes — the gram flour coating needs time to set and cling well. ingredients 400g paneer, cubed 1/2 cup thick yogurt, hung for 10 minutes to thicken 2 tbsp besan (gram flour (besan)), lightly roasted 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1 tsp ajwain (carom seeds (ajwain)) 1.5 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 1/2 tsp garam masala 1 tbsp mustard oil (sarson ka tel) salt to taste chaat masala & lemon wedges to finish method 1 preheat: when you reach the airfryer step, preheat it to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 in chef magic, whisk the hung yogurt with roasted besan, ginger-garlic paste, ajwain, chilli powder, garam masala, mustard oil and salt into a thick marinade. 3 coat the paneer cubes in the marinade and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. 4 skewer or arrange in the airfryer basket. 5 grill at 200°c for 14 minutes, turning once, until the coating is lightly charred and crisp at the edges. 6 dust with chaat masala and serve with lemon wedges and mint chutney. tip: roasting the besan for a minute before mixing it in removes the raw taste that can otherwise come through in the coating.

recipes.title: Paneer Manchurian (Gravy)
recipes.search: paneer manchurian (gravy) paneer manchurian (gravy) airfryer (fry the balls) → chef magic (make 200°c fry 14 min + sauce 10 min sauce) — serves 4 vegetarian • everyday • indo-chinese ingredients 250g paneer, grated 3 tbsp cornflour 2 tbsp maida (plain flour) 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste), divided salt to taste oil spray 1 onion, cubed 1 capsicum, cubed 2 tbsp soy sauce 1 tbsp chilli sauce 1 tbsp tomato ketchup 1 tbsp vinegar 1 cup vegetable stock or water 1 tsp cornflour, mixed with water, for the slurry spring onion greens to garnish method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 mix grated paneer with cornflour, maida, half the ginger-garlic paste and salt; shape into small balls. 3 spray the balls generously with oil and arrange in the airfryer basket. 4 air-fry at 200°c for 14 minutes, shaking halfway, until golden and firm. 5 in chef magic, add a little oil; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook onion and capsicum with the remaining ginger-garlic paste for 4 minutes. 6 add soy sauce, chilli sauce, ketchup, vinegar and stock; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and simmer for 3 minutes. 7 stir in the cornflour slurry and cook 2 minutes until glossy and thickened, then add the fried paneer balls and simmer gently for 2 minutes so they soak up some sauce without going soft. garnish with spring onion.

recipes.title: Paneer Bhurji (Dry, Standalone)
recipes.search: paneer bhurji (dry, standalone) paneer bhurji (dry, standalone) chef magic – sauté auto 15 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegetarian • high-protein • everyday ingredients 300g paneer, crumbled 1 onion, finely chopped 1 tomato, finely chopped 1 capsicum, finely chopped 1 green chilli (hari mirch), chopped 1/2 tsp cumin seeds (jeera) 1/4 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1/2 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 1/4 tsp garam masala 1 tbsp oil or butter salt to taste chopped coriander (dhania) to garnish method 1 add oil and cumin seeds to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) until they splutter. 2 add onion and green chilli; cook for 4 minutes until soft. 3 add capsicum and tomato; sauté 4 minutes until softened. 4 stir in turmeric, chilli powder and salt, then fold in the crumbled paneer; sauté gently for 5 minutes until just heated through. 5 sprinkle with garam masala and garnish with coriander before serving — with toast, in wraps, or alongside rotis. tip: add the paneer last and keep the heat gentle throughout — this dish is best soft and crumbly, not fried firm.

recipes.title: Paneer Cutlets
recipes.search: paneer cutlets paneer cutlets airfryer – fry 190°c 16 min — serves 4 (makes ~8) vegetarian • everyday prep ahead: chill the shaped cutlets for 15 minutes before air-frying so they hold together better. ingredients 250g paneer, grated 2 boiled potatoes, mashed 1/4 cup boiled peas & carrot, chopped 1 tsp ginger (adrak), grated 1 green chilli (hari mirch), chopped 1/2 tsp garam masala 2 tbsp cornflour 1 cup breadcrumbs salt to taste oil spray method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 190°c for 4 minutes before adding the food to the basket. 2 mix grated paneer, mashed potato, vegetables, ginger, chilli, garam masala, cornflour and salt into a firm dough. 3 shape into flat patties and chill for 15 minutes. 4 coat each patty in breadcrumbs, pressing gently so they stick. 5 spray with oil and arrange in a single layer in the basket. 6 air-fry at 190°c for 16 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden and crisp on both sides.

recipes.title: Paneer Momos
recipes.search: paneer momos paneer momos chef magic – steam auto 14 min — serves 4 (makes ~15) vegetarian • high-protein ingredients 15 momo wrappers 200g paneer, grated 1/4 cup finely chopped cabbage & carrot 1 spring onion, chopped 1 tsp soy sauce 1/2 tsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) salt & pepper to taste water for the steamer base method 1 mix grated paneer with vegetables, soy sauce, ginger-garlic paste, salt and pepper for the filling. 2 fill wrappers with the mixture and pleat closed. 3 add water to the jar, fit the steamer tray with momos on top. 4 select steam (100°c steam, paddle off) and cook for 14 minutes until wrappers turn glossy. 5 serve hot with a spicy chilli-garlic dip or mint chutney.

recipes.title: Dahi Paneer (Yogurt Paneer Curry)
recipes.search: dahi paneer (yogurt paneer curry) dahi paneer (yogurt paneer curry) chef magic – sauté auto 18 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegetarian • high-protein • everyday prep ahead: whisk the yogurt smooth before adding, and keep the heat gentle once it goes in — this prevents the gravy from ingredients 250g paneer, cubed 1 cup yogurt, whisked smooth 1 onion, finely chopped 1 tsp cumin seeds (jeera) 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1 tsp coriander powder (dhania powder) 1/2 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 1 tbsp besan (gram flour (besan)) 1 tbsp ghee salt to taste chopped coriander (dhania) to garnish method 1 add ghee and cumin seeds to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) until they splutter. 2 add onion and cook for 5 minutes until soft. 3 add turmeric, coriander powder and chilli powder; sauté 1 minute. 4 whisk the besan into the yogurt until lump-free, then stir it into the jar; select sauté (speed 1–2, ~100–110°c) and simmer gently for 8 minutes, stirring often, until slightly thickened. 5 add the paneer cubes and salt; sauté gently for 3 minutes until warmed through. garnish with coriander. tip: whisking besan into the yogurt before it goes into the hot jar is what keeps this gravy smooth instead of curdled.

recipes.title: Paneer Angara (Smoky Charred Paneer Curry)
recipes.search: paneer angara (smoky charred paneer curry) paneer angara (smoky charred paneer curry) airfryer (char paneer) → chef magic (make 200°c char 8 min + gravy 18 min gravy) — serves 4 gluten-free • vegetarian • high-protein • everyday ingredients 300g paneer, cubed 1 tbsp oil, for charring 2 onions, roughly chopped 3 tomatoes, chopped 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1.5 tsp kashmiri chilli powder (mirch powder) 1/2 tsp garam masala 1 tsp kasuri methi (dried fenugreek (methi)), crushed 2 tbsp cream 1 tbsp butter salt to taste a small piece of charcoal & a few drops of oil (optional, for a smoky finish) method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food to the basket. 2 toss the paneer cubes lightly in oil and air-fry at 200°c for 8 minutes, shaking once, until charred at the edges. 3 in chef magic, add butter; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook the onions for 6 minutes until golden. 4 add tomatoes and ginger-garlic paste; cook for 8 minutes until soft, then select whisk/blend (speed 8–10) to purée smooth. 5 return to sauté (speed 1–2, ~100–110°c); stir in chilli powder, garam masala and salt, and simmer 4 minutes. 6 add the charred paneer, cream and crushed kasuri methi; sauté gently for 3 minutes. for a traditional smoky finish, place a small piece of heated charcoal in a bowl in the centre of the curry, add a drop of oil, and cover for 1 minute before serving (optional, use tongs and care). tip: charring the paneer in the airfryer first is what gives angara its name and signature smoky edge — don’t skip straight to

recipes.title: Misal Pav
recipes.search: misal pav misal pav chef magic – sauté + boil auto 24 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegan • high-protein • maharashtrian prep ahead: sprout the moong beans 1–2 days ahead (soak overnight, then rest in a damp cloth until sprouted). ingredients 2 cups sprouted moong beans 1 onion, chopped 2 tomatoes, pureed 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 2 tbsp misal/goda masala (or garam masala) 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 2 tbsp oil 2 cups water salt to taste farsan (sev), chopped onion, lemon & pav, to serve method 1 add oil to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook onion for 5 minutes until golden. 2 add ginger-garlic paste, tomatoes, turmeric and misal masala; sauté for 7 minutes until the oil separates. 3 add the sprouted moong and water; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and cook for 10 minutes until sprouts are tender. 4 ladle into bowls and top generously with farsan, chopped onion and a squeeze of lemon; serve with pav.

recipes.title: Sabudana Khichdi
recipes.search: sabudana khichdi sabudana khichdi chef magic – sauté auto 16 min — serves 3 gluten-free • vegetarian • maharashtrian prep ahead: soak sabudana (tapioca pearls) in just enough water to cover for 4–6 hours or overnight until soft and separate. ingredients 2 cups sabudana, soaked 1/2 cup roasted peanuts, coarsely crushed 1 potato, diced 1 tsp cumin seeds (jeera) 2 green chillies (hari mirch), chopped 2 tbsp ghee salt to taste 1 tbsp lemon juice chopped coriander (dhania) method 1 add ghee and cumin seeds to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) until fragrant. 2 add the diced potato and green chillies; sauté for 5 minutes until potato softens. 3 add the soaked sabudana, crushed peanuts and salt; sauté gently for 8 minutes, stirring often, until translucent. 4 finish with lemon juice and coriander before serving. tip: sabudana turns gluey if over-soaked — it should be soft but still separate, not mushy, before cooking.

recipes.title: Kothimbir Vadi
recipes.search: kothimbir vadi kothimbir vadi chef magic (steam) → airfryer (fry, for a crisp finish) 190°c — steam 16 min + fry 8 min — makes ~16 gluten-free • vegan • maharashtrian ingredients 2 cups besan (gram flour (besan)) 1 cup chopped coriander leaves (hara dhania) 1 tsp ginger (adrak)-green chilli (hari mirch) paste 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1 tsp sesame seeds 1 tbsp oil, plus extra for frying salt to taste water as needed method 1 preheat: when you reach the airfryer step, preheat it to 190°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 mix besan, coriander, ginger-chilli paste, turmeric, sesame seeds, oil and salt with just enough water to form a thick, spreadable batter. 3 spread into a greased dish that fits the steamer tray, about 2cm thick. 4 steam in chef magic (100°c steam, paddle off) for 16 minutes until firm and a toothpick comes out clean; cool and cut into small squares or diamonds. 5 spray the pieces with oil and air-fry at 190°c for 8 minutes until golden and crisp.

recipes.title: Dal Baati (Baati Only)
recipes.search: dal baati (baati only) dal baati (baati only) airfryer – bake 190°c 28 min makes ~8 vegetarian • rajasthani prep ahead: rest the dough for 20 minutes before shaping so it firms up and holds together while baking. ingredients 2 cups whole wheat flour (coarse, if available) 1/2 cup semolina (sooji) 1/2 cup ghee, melted, plus extra for dunking 1/2 tsp baking soda salt to taste water as needed method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 190°c for 4 minutes before adding the food to the basket. 2 mix flour, semolina, melted ghee, baking soda and salt; add water gradually to form a firm, tight dough. rest 20 minutes. 3 divide into 8 balls, pressing each firmly so it doesn’t crack while baking. 4 arrange the balls in the basket, spaced apart. 5 bake at 190°c for 28 minutes, turning every 10 minutes, until deep golden and firm all over. 6 while still hot, dunk each baati briefly in melted ghee before serving with dal. tip: serve with the everyday toor dal or cholar dal recipe elsewhere in this book for the full dal-baati experience.

recipes.title: Gatte ki Sabzi
recipes.search: gatte ki sabzi gatte ki sabzi chef magic – boil then sauté auto 26 min — serves 4 vegetarian • rajasthani ingredients 1.5 cups besan (gram flour (besan)) 2 tbsp oil, divided 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi), divided salt to taste water as needed 1 cup yogurt, whisked 1 tsp cumin seeds (jeera) 1/2 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 1/2 tsp garam masala chopped coriander (dhania) method 1 mix besan, oil, turmeric and salt with water into a firm dough; roll into thin logs. 2 add water to the jar; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and cook the besan logs for 10 minutes until firm. cool slightly and slice into pieces (gatte). 3 add oil and cumin seeds to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) until fragrant, then add turmeric, chilli powder and whisked yogurt. 4 add the gatte pieces and simmer on sauté (speed 1–2, ~100–110°c) for 10 minutes, stirring gently, until the gravy thickens. sprinkle garam masala and garnish with coriander.

recipes.title: Dum Aloo (Kashmiri Style)
recipes.search: dum aloo (kashmiri style) dum aloo (kashmiri style) airfryer (fry potatoes) → chef magic (make 190°c fry 15 min + gravy 18 min gravy) — serves 4 gluten-free • vegetarian • kashmiri ingredients 500g baby potatoes, peeled and pricked 2 tbsp oil, divided 1/2 cup yogurt, whisked 1 tbsp kashmiri chilli powder (mirch powder) 1 tsp fennel (saunf) powder 1/2 tsp ginger (adrak) powder 1 bay leaf (tej patta) 1 tsp cumin seeds (jeera) salt to taste method 1 preheat: when you reach the airfryer step, preheat it to 190°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 toss the baby potatoes with oil and arrange in the airfryer basket. 3 air-fry at 190°c for 15 minutes, shaking halfway, until lightly golden and just tender. 4 in chef magic, add oil, bay leaf and cumin seeds; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) until fragrant. 5 add whisked yogurt, kashmiri chilli powder, fennel powder, ginger powder and salt; simmer on sauté (speed 1–2, ~100–110°c) for 8 minutes, stirring, until thick. 6 add the fried potatoes and simmer a further 5 minutes so they soak up the gravy.

recipes.title: Sarson ka Saag
recipes.search: sarson ka saag sarson ka saag chef magic – boil then sauté auto 32 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegan • punjabi • high-fibre ingredients 3 cups mustard greens (sarson), chopped 1 cup spinach, chopped 1 small onion, chopped 1 tomato, chopped 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 2 tbsp cornmeal (makki atta) 2 tbsp ghee 1 green chilli (hari mirch) salt to taste method 1 add mustard greens, spinach and a splash of water to the jar; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and cook for 12 minutes until fully wilted and soft. 2 select whisk/blend (speed 8–10) briefly to mash coarsely (not fully smooth); set aside. 3 add ghee to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook onion, tomato, ginger-garlic paste and green chilli for 8 minutes. 4 stir the mashed greens back in with cornmeal and salt; simmer on sauté (speed 1–2, ~100–110°c) for 8 minutes until thick. top with a spoon of ghee before serving.

recipes.title: Shahi Paneer
recipes.search: shahi paneer shahi paneer chef magic – sauté auto 22 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegetarian • high-protein • mughlai ingredients 200g paneer, cubed 1 onion, roughly chopped 15 cashews, soaked 1 tomato, chopped 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1/2 tsp garam masala 1/4 tsp nutmeg (jaiphal) powder 3 tbsp cream 2 tbsp ghee 1 tsp sugar salt to taste method 1 add ghee to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft. 2 add soaked cashews, tomato and ginger-garlic paste; cook for 6 minutes, then select whisk/blend (speed 8–10) to purée smooth. 3 return to sauté (speed 1–2, ~100–110°c); add garam masala, nutmeg, sugar and salt, and simmer for 5 minutes. 4 gently fold in the paneer cubes and cream; sauté 3 minutes just to warm through.

recipes.title: Mirchi ka Salan (Hyderabadi)
recipes.search: mirchi ka salan (hyderabadi) mirchi ka salan (hyderabadi) chef magic – sauté + boil auto 24 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegan • hyderabadi ingredients 8 large green chillies (hari mirch), slit 3 tbsp peanuts, roasted 2 tbsp sesame seeds, roasted 1 onion, chopped 1 tsp tamarind (imli) paste 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 2 tbsp oil salt to taste method 1 grind the roasted peanuts and sesame seeds with a little water into a smooth paste. 2 add oil to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook the onion for 6 minutes until golden, then add the green chillies and cook 4 minutes until blistered. 3 add the peanut-sesame paste, turmeric, tamarind paste and salt with a little water. 4 select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and cook for 10 minutes until the gravy thickens and coats the chillies.

recipes.title: Kerala Avial
recipes.search: kerala avial kerala avial chef magic – boil then sauté auto 24 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegetarian • kerala ingredients 3 cups mixed vegetables (carrot, beans, drumstick, raw banana), cut into batons 1/2 cup grated coconut 1/2 tsp cumin seeds (jeera) 2 green chillies (hari mirch) 1/2 cup yogurt 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 2 tbsp coconut oil 9 curry leaves (kadi patta) salt to taste method 1 add the mixed vegetables, turmeric and enough water to just cover to the jar; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and cook for 12 minutes until tender. 2 grind the grated coconut, cumin seeds and green chillies with a little water into a coarse paste. 3 stir the coconut paste and whisked yogurt into the cooked vegetables; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) briefly for 5 minutes to warm through without boiling hard. 4 finish with coconut oil and curry leaves; season with salt and serve.

recipes.title: Odia Dalma
recipes.search: odia dalma odia dalma chef magic – boil then sauté auto 26 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegan • high-fibre • odia ingredients 1 cup toor dal, washed 2 cups mixed vegetables (pumpkin, raw banana, potato, brinjal), chopped 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1 tsp panch phoron 2 dried red chillies (lal mirch) 1 tbsp ghee 3 cups water salt to taste method 1 add the dal, vegetables, turmeric and water to the jar; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and cook for 18 minutes until dal and vegetables are fully soft. 2 mash lightly with a spoon for a rustic texture. 3 add ghee, panch phoron and dried red chillies directly into the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) for 2 minutes to temper. 4 stir well and season with salt before serving.

recipes.title: Khandvi
recipes.search: khandvi khandvi chef magic – sauté auto 18 min — serves 4 gluten-free • vegetarian • gujarati • low-oil prep ahead: have a greased flat plate or tray ready before you start — the batter must be spread while still hot. ingredients 1 cup besan (gram flour (besan)) 1 cup yogurt 1.5 cups water 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1 tsp ginger (adrak)-green chilli (hari mirch) paste salt to taste 1 tsp mustard seeds (rai) 9 curry leaves (kadi patta) 1 tbsp oil grated coconut & chopped coriander (dhania) to garnish method 1 whisk besan, yogurt, water, turmeric, ginger-chilli paste and salt into a smooth, lump-free batter. 2 add to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook, stirring constantly, for 12 minutes until thick and no longer raw-tasting. 3 working quickly, spread the hot batter thinly onto a greased plate; cool slightly and cut into strips, then roll each up. 4 temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in hot oil; pour over the rolls and garnish with coconut and coriander. tip: spread the batter as soon as it’s cooked — it firms up fast and becomes hard to spread once it cools.

recipes.title: Chilli Paneer (Dry)
recipes.search: chilli paneer (dry) chilli paneer (dry) airfryer (fry paneer) → chef magic (toss in 200°c fry 14 min + toss 8 min sauce) — serves 4 vegetarian • everyday ingredients 250g paneer, cubed 3 tbsp cornflour, divided 2 tbsp maida (plain flour) 1 tbsp soy sauce, divided oil spray 1 capsicum, cubed 1 onion, cubed 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1 tbsp chilli sauce 1 tbsp vinegar 2 green chillies (hari mirch), slit 1/2 cup water mixed with 1 tsp cornflour method 1 preheat: when you reach the airfryer step, preheat it to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 toss the paneer cubes with cornflour, maida and half the soy sauce until coated. 3 spray the paneer with oil and air-fry at 200°c for 14 minutes, shaking halfway, until golden. 4 in chef magic, add a little oil; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook capsicum, onion, ginger-garlic paste and green chillies for 4 minutes. 5 add remaining soy sauce, chilli sauce, vinegar and the cornflour-water mix; cook 2 minutes until thickened. 6 toss in the fried paneer just before serving to keep it crisp.

recipes.title: Gobi Manchurian (Dry)
recipes.search: gobi manchurian (dry) gobi manchurian (dry) airfryer (fry the florets) → chef magic (toss in 200°c fry 15 min + toss 8 min sauce) — serves 4 vegan • everyday • indo-chinese prep ahead: pat the cauliflower florets fully dry after washing so the batter clings properly. ingredients 1 medium cauliflower, cut into florets 3 tbsp cornflour 2 tbsp maida (plain flour) 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste), divided salt to taste oil spray 1 onion, cubed 1 capsicum, cubed 2 tbsp soy sauce 1 tbsp chilli sauce 1 tbsp tomato ketchup 1 tbsp vinegar 1/2 cup water mixed with 1 tsp cornflour spring onion greens to garnish method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 toss the cauliflower florets with cornflour, maida, half the ginger-garlic paste, salt and a splash of water to form a light coating. 3 spray generously with oil and arrange in a single layer in the airfryer basket. 4 air-fry at 200°c for 15 minutes, shaking halfway, until golden and crisp. 5 in chef magic, add a little oil; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook onion and capsicum with the remaining ginger-garlic paste for 4 minutes. 6 add soy sauce, chilli sauce, ketchup, vinegar and the cornflour-water mix; cook 2 minutes until glossy and thickened. 7 toss in the fried cauliflower just before serving so it stays crisp; garnish with spring onion. tip: toss the florets in the sauce only at the very last minute — sitting in sauce too long turns the crisp coating soggy.

recipes.title: Vegetable Manchurian Gravy
recipes.search: vegetable manchurian gravy vegetable manchurian gravy airfryer (fry the balls) → chef magic (make 200°c fry 15 min + gravy 12 min gravy) — serves 4 vegan • everyday • indo-chinese ingredients 2 cups finely shredded cabbage, carrot & capsicum 3 tbsp cornflour 2 tbsp maida (plain flour) 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste), divided salt to taste oil spray 1 onion, chopped 2 tbsp soy sauce 1 tbsp chilli sauce 1 tbsp tomato ketchup 1 tbsp vinegar 2 cups vegetable stock or water 2 tsp cornflour, mixed with water, for the slurry spring onion greens to garnish method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 mix shredded vegetables with cornflour, maida, half the ginger-garlic paste and salt; shape into small balls. 3 spray the balls generously with oil and arrange in the airfryer basket. 4 air-fry at 200°c for 15 minutes, shaking halfway, until golden and crisp. 5 in chef magic, add a little oil; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook the onion with the remaining ginger-garlic paste for 3 minutes. 6 add soy sauce, chilli sauce, ketchup, vinegar and stock; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and simmer for 4 minutes. 7 stir in the cornflour slurry and cook 3 minutes until the gravy turns glossy and slightly thick, then add the fried balls and simmer gently for 2 minutes so they soften just slightly in the gravy. garnish with spring onion. tip: unlike the dry version, the balls are meant to soak a little here — a thin, silky gravy is the goal, not a thick one.

recipes.title: Chilli Mushroom (Dry)
recipes.search: chilli mushroom (dry) chilli mushroom (dry) airfryer (fry mushrooms) → chef magic (toss 200°c fry 12 min + toss 8 min in sauce) — serves 4 vegan • everyday • indo-chinese ingredients 300g button mushrooms, halved 3 tbsp cornflour 2 tbsp maida (plain flour) 1 tbsp soy sauce, divided oil spray 1 capsicum, cubed 1 onion, cubed 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1 tbsp chilli sauce 1 tbsp vinegar 2 green chillies (hari mirch), slit 1/2 cup water mixed with 1 tsp cornflour method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 toss the mushrooms with cornflour, maida and half the soy sauce until lightly coated. 3 spray with oil and arrange in a single layer in the airfryer basket. 4 air-fry at 200°c for 12 minutes, shaking halfway, until golden. 5 in chef magic, add a little oil; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook capsicum, onion, ginger-garlic paste and green chillies for 4 minutes. 6 add remaining soy sauce, chilli sauce, vinegar and the cornflour-water mix; cook 2 minutes until thickened. 7 toss in the fried mushrooms just before serving to keep them from turning rubbery. tip: mushrooms release water as they cook — air-frying them first (instead of adding raw to the sauce) is what keeps this dish

recipes.title: Chilli Gobi (Dry)
recipes.search: chilli gobi (dry) chilli gobi (dry) airfryer (fry the florets) → chef magic (toss in 200°c fry 15 min + toss 8 min sauce) — serves 4 vegan • everyday • indo-chinese ingredients 1 medium cauliflower, cut into florets 3 tbsp cornflour 2 tbsp maida (plain flour) 1/2 tsp black pepper (kali mirch) salt to taste oil spray 1 capsicum, cubed 1 onion, cubed 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 4–5 dried red chillies (lal mirch) 1 tbsp soy sauce 1 tbsp chilli sauce 1 tsp vinegar 1/4 cup water mixed with 1 tsp cornflour method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 toss the cauliflower florets with cornflour, maida, black pepper, salt and a splash of water to form a light coating. 3 spray with oil and arrange in a single layer in the airfryer basket. 4 air-fry at 200°c for 15 minutes, shaking halfway, until golden and crisp. 5 in chef magic, add a little oil; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook capsicum, onion, ginger-garlic paste and dried red chillies for 4 minutes. 6 add soy sauce, chilli sauce, vinegar and the cornflour-water mix; cook 2 minutes until thickened and glossy. 7 toss in the fried florets just before serving; serve immediately while still crisp. tip: chilli gobi differs from gobi manchurian mainly in the sharper black pepper and dried red chilli heat — keep the sauce light

recipes.title: Vegetable Hakka Noodles
recipes.search: vegetable hakka noodles vegetable hakka noodles chef magic – boil then sauté auto 20 min — serves 3 vegan • everyday • indo-chinese prep ahead: rinse the boiled noodles under cold water and toss with a little oil to stop them sticking together. ingredients 200g hakka or thin noodles 1 cup thinly sliced mixed vegetables (cabbage, carrot, capsicum, beans) 2 spring onions, sliced (whites and greens separated) 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 2 tbsp soy sauce 1 tsp vinegar 1 tsp chilli sauce (optional) 2 tbsp oil salt & pepper to taste method 1 add water and a pinch of salt to the jar; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and cook the noodles until just done, about 6 minutes; drain, rinse in cold water, and toss with a little oil. 2 add oil to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook the spring onion whites and ginger-garlic paste for 3 minute. 4 add the mixed vegetables and sauté for 5 minutes, keeping them crisp-tender. 5 add the noodles, soy sauce, vinegar, chilli sauce and pepper; toss on sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) for 5 minutes until well combined and lightly charred in places. 6 garnish with spring onion greens and serve hot. tip: high heat and quick tossing is what gives hakka noodles their signature wok-charred flavour — don’t let them sit and

recipes.title: Vegetable Manchow Soup
recipes.search: vegetable manchow soup vegetable manchow soup chef magic – sauté + boil auto 20 min — serves 4 vegan • everyday • indo-chinese ingredients 1/2 cup finely chopped mixed vegetables (carrot, beans, cabbage, capsicum) 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 2 tbsp soy sauce 1 tsp chilli sauce 1 tsp vinegar 4 cups vegetable stock or water 2 tbsp cornflour, mixed with water, for the slurry 2 tbsp oil salt & pepper to taste fried noodles, spring onion greens, to garnish method 1 add oil to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook the ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute. 2 add the chopped vegetables and sauté for 5 minutes. 3 add stock, soy sauce, chilli sauce and vinegar; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and simmer for 8 minutes. 4 stir in the cornflour slurry and cook a further 4 minutes until the soup turns glossy and slightly thickened. season with salt and pepper. 5 ladle into bowls and top with crispy fried noodles and spring onion greens. tip: the crunchy fried noodles on top are what make this a manchow soup rather than a plain vegetable soup — don’t skip

recipes.title: Schezwan Fried Rice
