recipes.search: chicken biryani (dum-style) chicken biryani (dum-style) chef magic (cook rice + gravy) → airfryer (dum finish) 160°c — 45 min — serves 4 gluten-free • high-protein • everyday prep ahead: marinate the chicken in yogurt and spices for at least 30 minutes (longer is better). ingredients 500g chicken, curry-cut pieces 1/2 cup thick yogurt 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1 tsp biryani masala 2 cups basmati rice, soaked 20 minutes 2 onions, thinly sliced 2 tomatoes, chopped 2 green chillies (hari mirch), slit 1/4 cup mint leaves, chopped 1/4 cup coriander leaves (hara dhania), chopped 3 tbsp ghee or oil 1 tsp shahi jeera (caraway) or cumin seeds (jeera) 2 bay leaves (tej patta), 4 cloves (laung), 1 cinnamon stick (dalchini) salt to taste a few strands of saffron (kesar) soaked in 2 tbsp warm milk (optional) method 1 marinate the chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chilli powder, turmeric and biryani masala for at least 30 minutes. 2 in chef magic, add ghee; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and fry the onions until deep golden. set half aside for garnish. 3 add shahi jeera, bay leaves, cloves and cinnamon; sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. 4 add tomatoes and green chillies; cook for 4 minutes until soft. 5 add the marinated chicken and cook on sauté for 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is half-cooked and the oil separates. 6 add the soaked rice, 3 cups hot water, salt, mint and coriander; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and cook covered for 12 minutes until the rice is just tender and water is absorbed. 7 transfer to an airfryer-safe dish, drizzle with saffron milk and top with the reserved fried onions. 8 cover tightly and airfryer-dum at 160°c for 10 minutes to let the flavours settle before serving. tip: resist stirring the rice once it goes in — biryani rice should stay in separate, fluffy grains, not turn mushy.

recipes.title: Chicken Korma
recipes.search: chicken korma chicken korma chef magic – sauté + boil auto 32 min — serves 4 gluten-free • high-protein • mughlai • everyday prep ahead: soak 15 cashews in warm water for 15 minutes for a smoother gravy. ingredients 500g chicken, curry-cut pieces 1/2 cup yogurt 15 cashews, soaked 2 onions, sliced 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1 tsp coriander powder (dhania powder) 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1/2 tsp garam masala 2 green cardamom (elaichi), 1 cinnamon stick (dalchini) 3 tbsp ghee or oil 1/4 cup cream salt to taste coriander leaves (hara dhania) to garnish method 1 in chef magic, add ghee; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and fry the onions until golden. blend with the soaked cashews and a splash of water into a smooth paste; set aside. 2 add a little more ghee to the jar with cardamom and cinnamon; sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. 3 add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute, then add the chicken; sauté for 6 minutes until lightly browned. 4 add coriander powder, turmeric and salt; cook for 2 minutes. 5 stir in the onion-cashew paste and 1/2 cup water; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and simmer covered for 15 minutes until the chicken is tender. 6 whisk in the yogurt off direct heat to prevent splitting, then return to sauté (speed 1–2) for 3 minutes. 7 stir in cream and garam masala; simmer for 2 minutes and garnish with coriander before serving. tip: korma should be pale and creamy, not red — skip the chilli powder and let the cashew paste carry the richness.

recipes.title: Ghar ka Chicken Curry (Simple Home-Style)
recipes.search: ghar ka chicken curry (simple home-style) ghar ka chicken curry (simple home-style) chef magic – sauté + boil auto 30 min — serves 4 gluten-free • high-protein • everyday ingredients 500g chicken, curry-cut pieces 2 onions, finely chopped 2 tomatoes, chopped 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1 tsp coriander powder (dhania powder) 1/2 tsp garam masala 3 tbsp oil 1 tsp cumin seeds (jeera) salt to taste coriander leaves (hara dhania) to garnish method 1 in chef magic, add oil; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and crackle the cumin seeds for 30 seconds. 2 add onions and cook for 7 minutes until golden. 3 add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute, then add tomatoes, chilli powder, turmeric, coriander powder and salt; cook for 6 minutes until the oil separates. 4 add the chicken and sauté for 5 minutes until it changes colour and coats in the masala. 5 add 1 cup water; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and simmer covered for 12 minutes until the chicken is cooked through. 6 sprinkle garam masala and coriander leaves before serving. tip: this is the everyday, no-frills version — thinner gravy, simple spices, and best eaten with plain steamed rice or rotis.

recipes.title: Kadai Chicken
recipes.search: kadai chicken kadai chicken chef magic – sauté + boil auto 28 min — serves 4 gluten-free • high-protein • everyday ingredients 500g chicken, boneless or curry-cut 2 onions, cubed 2 capsicums, cubed 2 tomatoes, pureed 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1 tbsp kadai masala (coriander seeds (sookha dhania) + dried red chillies (lal mirch), crushed) 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 3 tbsp oil salt to taste coriander leaves (hara dhania) to garnish method 1 in chef magic, add oil; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook onions for 3 minutes until just translucent. 2 add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute, then add the chicken; sauté for 6 minutes until lightly browned. 3 add tomato puree, kadai masala, turmeric and salt; cook for 6 minutes until the oil separates. 4 add 1/2 cup water; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and simmer covered for 10 minutes until the chicken is nearly cooked. 5 add the capsicum and continue on sauté (speed 2–4) for 4 minutes until just tender-crisp. 6 garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot. tip: keep the capsicum in big cubes and add it late — it should stay crunchy, not go soft.

recipes.title: Chicken Saag (Chicken with Spinach)
recipes.search: chicken saag (chicken with spinach) chicken saag (chicken with spinach) chef magic – sauté + boil auto 30 min — serves 4 gluten-free • high-protein • everyday ingredients 500g chicken, boneless, cubed 400g spinach, roughly chopped 1 onion, chopped 2 tomatoes, chopped 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1–2 green chillies (hari mirch) 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1 tsp coriander powder (dhania powder) 1/2 tsp garam masala 3 tbsp oil or ghee 2 tbsp cream (optional) salt to taste method 1 in chef magic, add a splash of water; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and blanch the spinach with green chillies for 3 minutes. blend to a smooth puree; set aside. 2 add oil to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook the onion for 5 minutes until golden. 3 add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute, then add tomatoes, turmeric, coriander powder and salt; cook for 5 minutes until soft. 4 add the chicken and sauté for 6 minutes until lightly browned and coated in the masala. 5 stir in the spinach puree and 1/4 cup water; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and simmer covered for 10 minutes until the chicken is cooked through. 6 stir in garam masala and cream if using; simmer for 2 minutes before serving. tip: blanching the spinach briefly (rather than raw-blending it) keeps the saag a deep green instead of turning muddy.

recipes.title: Chicken Keema (Minced Chicken Curry)
recipes.search: chicken keema (minced chicken curry) chicken keema (minced chicken curry) chef magic – sauté + boil auto 26 min — serves 4 gluten-free • high-protein • everyday ingredients 500g minced chicken (keema) 1 onion, finely chopped 2 tomatoes, chopped 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1/2 cup green peas 1 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1 tsp coriander powder (dhania powder) 1/2 tsp garam masala 3 tbsp oil 1 tsp cumin seeds (jeera) salt to taste coriander leaves (hara dhania) to garnish method 1 in chef magic, add oil; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and crackle the cumin seeds for 30 seconds. 2 add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until golden. 3 add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute, then add tomatoes, chilli powder, turmeric, coriander powder and salt; cook for 5 minutes until soft. 4 add the minced chicken, breaking up any lumps, and sauté for 8 minutes until it changes colour and no longer looks pink. 5 add the peas and 1/2 cup water; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and simmer covered for 8 minutes until the keema is cooked through and the peas are tender. 6 sprinkle garam masala and coriander leaves before serving. tip: great with pav or as a quick paratha filling — it also freezes well for a fast weeknight dinner.

recipes.title: Chicken Do Pyaza
recipes.search: chicken do pyaza chicken do pyaza chef magic – sauté + boil auto 30 min — serves 4 gluten-free • high-protein • everyday ingredients 500g chicken, curry-cut pieces 3 onions — 2 sliced, 1 cubed into petals 2 tomatoes, chopped 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1 tsp coriander powder (dhania powder) 1/2 tsp garam masala 3 tbsp oil salt to taste coriander leaves (hara dhania) to garnish method 1 in chef magic, add oil; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook the sliced onions for 8 minutes until deep golden. blend to a smooth paste with a splash of water; set aside. 2 add a little more oil to the jar; sauté the onion petals for 3 minutes until just softened and lightly charred at the edges. set aside for garnish. 3 add ginger-garlic paste to the jar and cook for 1 minute, then add tomatoes, chilli powder, turmeric, coriander powder and salt; cook for 5 minutes until the oil separates. 4 stir in the onion paste, then add the chicken; sauté for 6 minutes until well coated and lightly browned. 5 add 1 cup water; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and simmer covered for 12 minutes until the chicken is cooked through. 6 fold in the reserved onion petals and garam masala; simmer for 2 minutes and garnish with coriander before serving. tip: 'do pyaza' means double onion — the smooth onion paste builds the base, and the petals on top add bite and colour.

recipes.title: Amritsari Fried Chicken (Punjabi-Style)
recipes.search: amritsari fried chicken (punjabi-style) amritsari fried chicken (punjabi-style) chef magic (mix marinade) → airfryer 200°c marinate 30 min + fry 18 min — serves 4 high-protein • everyday prep ahead: marinate the chicken for at least 30 minutes (overnight deepens the flavour). ingredients 500g chicken (curry-cut, bone-in works best) 1/2 cup yogurt 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1 tsp carom seeds (ajwain) 1 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1 tsp garam masala 1 tbsp lemon juice 1/2 cup besan (gram flour (besan)) 2 tbsp cornflour 1 egg salt to taste oil spray method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 in chef magic, mix the yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, ajwain, chilli powder, turmeric, garam masala, lemon juice and salt into a marinade. 3 coat the chicken well and marinate for at least 30 minutes. 4 whisk the besan, cornflour and egg into the marinated chicken to form a thick, clingy coating. 5 spray generously with oil and arrange in a single layer in the airfryer basket. 6 air-fry at 200°c for 18 minutes, shaking the basket halfway, until deeply golden and crisp on the outside. tip: the carom seeds are what make this taste properly amritsari — don't swap them out, they cut through the fry and settle the stomach too.

recipes.title: Chicken Karahi (Punjabi Wok-Style)
recipes.search: chicken karahi (punjabi wok-style) chicken karahi (punjabi wok-style) chef magic – sauté auto 24 min — serves 4 gluten-free • high-protein • everyday ingredients 500g chicken, curry-cut pieces 4 tomatoes, chopped 2 green chillies (hari mirch), slit 1 tbsp ginger (adrak), julienned (plus extra to garnish) 1 tbsp garlic (lehsun), finely chopped 1 tsp coriander seeds (sookha dhania), crushed 1 tsp red chilli (lal mirch) flakes 3 tbsp oil or ghee 1/2 tsp garam masala 1 tbsp kasuri methi (dried fenugreek (methi)), crushed salt to taste coriander leaves (hara dhania) to garnish method 1 in chef magic, add oil; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook the garlic for 1 minute until fragrant, without browning. 2 add the chicken and sauté for 7 minutes on high (speed 3–4) until lightly seared on the outside. 3 add the tomatoes, green chillies, crushed coriander seeds, chilli flakes and salt; cook on sauté (speed 2–4) for 10 minutes, mashing the tomatoes down, until the oil separates and the masala turns thick and dry-ish. 4 add half the ginger julienne and cook for 4 minutes more until the chicken is cooked through and the karahi is fairly dry, not gravy-like. 5 sprinkle garam masala and kasuri methi; toss for 1 minute. 6 garnish with the remaining ginger julienne and coriander leaves before serving. tip: karahi is meant to be cooked hot and fast with no added water — let the tomatoes' own moisture do the work so the masala stays thick and clingy.

recipes.title: Punjabi Dhaba-Style Murgh Curry (Bone-In)
recipes.search: punjabi dhaba-style murgh curry (bone-in) punjabi dhaba-style murgh curry (bone-in) chef magic – sauté + boil auto 34 min — serves 4 gluten-free • high-protein • everyday prep ahead: bone-in chicken gives the best flavour here — ask for curry-cut pieces with bone. ingredients 600g chicken, bone-in curry-cut pieces 2 onions, finely chopped 3 tomatoes, chopped 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1 tsp coriander powder (dhania powder) 1 tsp garam masala 4 tbsp mustard oil (sarson ka tel) 1 bay leaf (tej patta), 2 cloves (laung), 1 black cardamom (elaichi) salt to taste coriander leaves (hara dhania) to garnish method 1 in chef magic, add mustard oil; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and heat until it just starts to smoke, then let it settle for 30 seconds — this takes the rawness out of the oil. 2 add the bay leaf, cloves and black cardamom; sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. 3 add onions and cook for 8 minutes until deep golden. 4 add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute, then add tomatoes, chilli powder, turmeric, coriander powder and salt; cook for 8 minutes until the oil separates. 5 add the chicken and sauté for 6 minutes until well coated and lightly browned. 6 add 1.5 cups water; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and simmer covered for 15 minutes until the chicken is falling-off-the-bone tender. 7 sprinkle garam masala and coriander leaves before serving with tandoori roti. tip: this is the heavier, ghee-and-mustard-oil dhaba cousin of an everyday chicken curry — bone-in pieces and a longer simmer are what give it that roadside-stall depth.

recipes.title: Chicken Changezi
recipes.search: chicken changezi chicken changezi chef magic (grill marinade) → airfryer 200°c grill 15 min → chef magic gravy 18 min — serves 4 gluten-free • high-protein • everyday prep ahead: marinate the chicken for at least 30 minutes before grilling. ingredients 500g boneless chicken, cubed 1/2 cup yogurt 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 2 onions, sliced 2 tomatoes, chopped 10 cashews, soaked 1 tbsp chopped mixed dry fruits (almonds, raisins) 1 tsp coriander powder (dhania powder) 1 tsp garam masala 3 tbsp ghee or oil 1/4 cup cream salt to taste coriander leaves (hara dhania) to garnish method 1 preheat: when you reach the airfryer step, preheat it to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 mix the chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chilli powder, turmeric and salt; marinate for at least 30 minutes. 3 arrange the chicken in a single layer in the airfryer basket and grill at 200°c for 15 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges and cooked through. 4 meanwhile, in chef magic, add ghee; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and fry the onions until golden. blend with the soaked cashews and a splash of water into a smooth paste. 5 return the paste to the jar with tomatoes, coriander powder and salt; cook on sauté for 8 minutes until the oil separates. 6 add the grilled chicken and 1/2 cup water; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and simmer for 6 minutes. 7 stir in cream, garam masala and chopped dry fruits; simmer for 2 minutes and garnish with coriander before serving. tip: grilling the chicken first (rather than boiling it straight in the gravy) is what gives changezi its char and keeps the dry-fruit gravy from turning watery.

recipes.title: Kukkad Rassa (Kolhapuri Chicken Curry)
recipes.search: kukkad rassa (kolhapuri chicken curry) kukkad rassa (kolhapuri chicken curry) chef magic – sauté + boil auto 34 min — serves 4 gluten-free • high-protein • everyday prep ahead: dry-roast the kolhapuri masala spices ahead of time and let them cool before blending. ingredients 500g chicken, curry-cut pieces 1/2 cup grated dry coconut (kopra) 2 onions — 1 sliced, 1 chopped 6–8 dried kashmiri red chillies (lal mirch) (for colour, moderate heat) 4–5 dried spicy red chillies (lal mirch) (adjust to taste) 1 tbsp coriander seeds (sookha dhania) 1 tsp cumin seeds (jeera) 4 cloves (laung), 1 inch cinnamon (dalchini), 2 black cardamom (elaichi) 1 tbsp poppy seeds (khus khus) 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 2 tomatoes, chopped 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 3 tbsp oil salt to taste coriander leaves (hara dhania) to garnish method 1 in chef magic, dry-roast the coconut, dried red chillies, coriander seeds, cumin seeds, cloves, cinnamon, black cardamom and poppy seeds on sauté (speed 1–2, low heat) for 4 minutes, stirring often, until fragrant and lightly darkened. cool slightly, then blend to a coarse masala paste with a little water — this is your kolhapuri masala. 2 add oil to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook the sliced onion until deep golden brown, almost caramelised, about 8 minutes. 3 add the chopped onion, ginger-garlic paste and tomatoes; cook for 6 minutes until soft. 4 add the kolhapuri masala paste and turmeric; cook for 4 minutes until the oil separates and the raw smell disappears. 5 add the chicken and sauté for 6 minutes until well coated. 6 add 1.5 cups water and salt; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and simmer covered for 15 minutes until the chicken is tender and the curry is fiery red. 7 garnish with coriander leaves and serve with rice bhakri or steamed rice. tip: this is the 'tambda rassa' — deliberately thin, deep red and fiery. if it's too hot, spoon some of the oil off the top rather than adding cream; cream isn't traditional here.

recipes.title: Tandoori Grilled Chicken
recipes.search: tandoori grilled chicken tandoori grilled chicken chef magic (mix marinade) → airfryer 200°c marinate 1 hr + grill 22 min — serves 4 gluten-free • high-protein • everyday prep ahead: marinate the chicken for at least 1 hour, or overnight in the fridge for the best flavour and colour. ingredients 800g chicken (leg and thigh pieces, or a whole small chicken spatchcocked), skin scored 1 cup thick curd (hung yogurt) 2 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1 tbsp kashmiri red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 1 tsp turmeric powder (haldi) 1 tsp garam masala 1 tsp roasted cumin powder (bhuna jeera powder) 1 tsp coriander powder (dhania powder) 2 tbsp mustard oil (or vegetable oil) 1 tbsp lemon juice salt to taste lemon wedges and sliced onions, to serve method 1 preheat: when you reach the airfryer step, preheat it to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 in chef magic, blend the curd, ginger-garlic paste, chilli powder, turmeric, garam masala, cumin powder, coriander powder, mustard oil, lemon juice and salt into a smooth marinade. 3 score the chicken pieces deeply so the marinade penetrates, then coat thoroughly in the marinade. cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, or overnight. 4 arrange the chicken in a single layer in the airfryer basket, leaving space between pieces for even grilling. 5 grill at 200°c for 22 minutes, turning halfway, until the edges are charred and the chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°c). 6 rest for 5 minutes, then serve hot with lemon wedges and sliced onions. tip: a squeeze of fresh lemon and a light brushing of butter or ghee right after grilling gives the classic smoky tandoor finish, even without charcoal.

recipes.title: Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)
recipes.search: butter chicken (murgh makhani) butter chicken (murgh makhani) airfryer (grill chicken) → chef magic (make 200°c grill 16 min + gravy 20 min gravy) — serves 4 gluten-free • high-protein • mughlai • everyday prep ahead: marinate the chicken in yogurt and spices for at least 30 minutes (longer is better) before grilling. ingredients 500g boneless chicken, cubed 1/2 cup yogurt 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 1/2 tsp garam masala 3 tomatoes, pureed 15 cashews, soaked 3 tbsp butter 2 tbsp cream 1 tsp sugar 1 tsp kasuri methi (dried fenugreek (methi)) salt to taste method 1 preheat: when you reach the airfryer step, preheat it to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 marinate the chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chilli powder and garam masala for at least 30 minutes. 3 arrange the chicken in the airfryer basket and grill at 200°c for 16 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges. 4 in chef magic, add butter; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook pureed tomatoes with soaked cashews for 10 minutes, then select whisk/blend (speed 8–10) to purée smooth. 5 return to sauté (speed 1–2, ~100–110°c), add sugar, kasuri methi and salt; simmer 4 minutes, then add the grilled chicken and cream, simmering a further 6 minutes.

recipes.title: Chettinad Chicken
recipes.search: chettinad chicken chettinad chicken chef magic – sauté + boil auto 28 min — serves 4 gluten-free • high-protein • chettinad ingredients 500g chicken, curry cut 1 tbsp coriander seeds (sookha dhania) 1 tsp fennel seeds (saunf) 4 dried red chillies (lal mirch) 1/2 tsp peppercorns 2 tbsp grated coconut 1 onion, chopped 1 tomato, chopped 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 3 tbsp oil 9 curry leaves (kadi patta) salt to taste method 1 dry-roast coriander seeds, fennel seeds, dried red chillies, peppercorns and coconut briefly, then grind with a little water into a paste. 2 add oil and curry leaves to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook the onion for 6 minutes until golden. 3 add ginger-garlic paste and tomato; cook 5 minutes, then add the ground masala paste and cook 3 minutes until fragrant. 4 add the chicken and salt; sauté 6 minutes to sear, then select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and cook covered for 8 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the gravy thickens.

recipes.title: Goan Fish Curry (Air Fryer-Seared)
recipes.search: goan fish curry (air fryer-seared) goan fish curry (air fryer-seared) airfryer (sear the fish) → chef magic (make the 200°c sear 8 min + curry 18 min curry) — serves 4 gluten-free • high-protein prep ahead: marinate the fish in a little turmeric, chilli powder and salt for 15 minutes before searing. ingredients 500g firm fish fillets (pomfret, kingfish or basa), cut into large pieces 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder), divided 1 onion, chopped 1 tomato, chopped 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1 cup coconut milk 1 tbsp tamarind (imli) paste 9 curry leaves (kadi patta) 2 tbsp coconut oil salt to taste oil spray method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food to the basket. 2 rub the fish pieces with turmeric, half the chilli powder and salt; rest 15 minutes. 3 spray the fish lightly with oil and arrange in a single layer in the basket. 4 grill at 200°c for 8 minutes, turning once, until lightly seared and firm but not fully cooked through. 5 meanwhile, add coconut oil and curry leaves to chef magic’s jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft. 6 add ginger-garlic paste, tomato and the remaining chilli powder; sauté for 5 minutes until the tomato breaks down. 7 add the coconut milk and tamarind paste; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and simmer for 5 minutes. 8 gently slide in the seared fish and simmer a further 5 minutes, stirring as little as possible, until just cooked through. tip: searing the fish first means it only needs a brief, gentle simmer in the curry — that’s what keeps the pieces intact instead

recipes.title: Rui Macher Jhol (Light Bengali Rohu Curry)
recipes.search: rui macher jhol (light bengali rohu curry) rui macher jhol (light bengali rohu curry) chef magic – sauté + boil auto 22 min — serves 4 gluten-free • high-protein • bengali • everyday prep ahead: rub the fish pieces with a little turmeric and salt and let them sit for 10 minutes before frying. ingredients 6 pieces rohu (rui) fish 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi), plus extra for rubbing 2 potatoes, cut into wedges 1 tomato, chopped 1 tsp cumin seeds (jeera) 1/2 tsp nigella seeds (kalonji) 1 tsp cumin (jeera)-coriander powder (dhania powder) 1–2 green chillies (hari mirch), slit 3 tbsp mustard oil (sarson ka tel) salt to taste coriander leaves (hara dhania) to garnish method 1 rub the fish pieces with turmeric and salt; let sit for 10 minutes. 2 in chef magic, add mustard oil; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and shallow-fry the fish pieces for 2 minutes per side until lightly golden. remove and set aside. 3 in the same oil, crackle the cumin and nigella seeds for 30 seconds. 4 add the potato wedges and fry for 5 minutes until lightly golden at the edges. 5 add the tomato, turmeric, cumin-coriander powder, green chillies and salt; cook for 4 minutes until the tomato softens. 6 add 2 cups water; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and simmer covered for 8 minutes until the potatoes are nearly tender. 7 slide the fried fish back in and simmer for 4 minutes more, spooning the thin gravy over the top without stirring hard. 8 garnish with coriander leaves and serve with steamed rice. tip: jhol is meant to be thin and brothy, not thick — this is the everyday, light version of bengali fish curry, not a special-occasion one.

recipes.title: Sorshe Rui (Rohu in Mustard Gravy)
recipes.search: sorshe rui (rohu in mustard gravy) sorshe rui (rohu in mustard gravy) chef magic – sauté + boil auto 18 min — serves 4 gluten-free • high-protein • bengali • everyday prep ahead: soak the mustard seeds in warm water for 20 minutes before grinding — this takes the bitterness out. ingredients 6 pieces rohu (rui) fish 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi), plus extra for rubbing 3 tbsp yellow mustard seeds (rai), soaked 1–2 green chillies (hari mirch), plus extra to garnish 1/2 tsp nigella seeds (kalonji) 4 tbsp mustard oil (sarson ka tel) salt to taste method 1 rub the fish pieces with turmeric and salt; let sit for 10 minutes. 2 blend the soaked mustard seeds with the green chillies, a pinch of salt and a splash of water into a smooth paste. 3 in chef magic, add mustard oil; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and shallow-fry the fish pieces for 2 minutes per side until lightly golden. remove and set aside. 4 in the same oil, crackle the nigella seeds for 30 seconds. 5 add the mustard paste, turmeric and 1 cup water; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and simmer for 4 minutes, stirring gently. 6 slide the fried fish back in, top with slit green chillies and simmer for 4 minutes more without stirring hard. 7 finish with a drizzle of raw mustard oil and serve with steamed rice. tip: never over-boil a mustard gravy — it turns bitter. keep the simmer gentle and short once the paste goes in.

recipes.title: Rui Maach Bhaja (Crispy Airfried Rohu Fry)
recipes.search: rui maach bhaja (crispy airfried rohu fry) rui maach bhaja (crispy airfried rohu fry) airfryer – marinate 15 min + fry 200°c 12 min — serves 4 gluten-free • high-protein • bengali • everyday prep ahead: marinate the fish for at least 15 minutes before frying. ingredients 6 pieces rohu (rui) fish 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1/2 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 1 tsp lemon juice 2 tbsp rice flour or semolina (for the crust) salt to taste mustard oil (sarson ka tel) spray method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 rub the fish pieces with turmeric, chilli powder, lemon juice and salt; marinate for at least 15 minutes. 3 coat each piece lightly in rice flour or semolina, pressing gently so it sticks. 4 spray generously with mustard oil and arrange in a single layer in the airfryer basket. 5 air-fry at 200°c for 12 minutes, flipping halfway, until crisp and golden on both sides. 6 serve hot with a squeeze of lemon and sliced onions. tip: a light dusting of rice flour rather than a thick batter keeps this true to the classic bengali maach bhaja — thin, crisp, and not deep-fried heavy.

recipes.title: Catla Macher Kalia (Rich Bengali Catla Curry)
recipes.search: catla macher kalia (rich bengali catla curry) catla macher kalia (rich bengali catla curry) chef magic – sauté + boil auto 28 min — serves 4 gluten-free • high-protein • bengali • everyday prep ahead: rub the fish pieces with turmeric and salt and let them sit for 10 minutes before frying. ingredients 6 pieces catla fish 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi), plus extra for rubbing 1 onion, finely chopped or pasted 1 tbsp ginger (adrak) paste 1 tsp garlic (lehsun) paste 1 tomato, chopped 1/2 cup yogurt, whisked 1 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 1 tsp cumin (jeera)-coriander powder (dhania powder) 1/2 tsp garam masala 1 bay leaf (tej patta), 2 cloves (laung), 1 inch cinnamon (dalchini), 2 green cardamom (elaichi) 1/2 tsp sugar 4 tbsp mustard oil (sarson ka tel) salt to taste method 1 rub the fish pieces with turmeric and salt; let sit for 10 minutes. 2 in chef magic, add mustard oil; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and shallow-fry the fish pieces for 2 minutes per side until golden. remove and set aside. 3 in the same oil, add the bay leaf, cloves, cinnamon and cardamom; sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. 4 add the onion paste and cook for 6 minutes until golden. 5 add ginger paste, garlic paste and tomato; cook for 4 minutes until soft. 6 add chilli powder, cumin-coriander powder, turmeric and sugar; cook for 2 minutes, then whisk in the yogurt off direct heat and stir through. 7 add 1 cup water; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and simmer for 6 minutes until the gravy thickens slightly. 8 slide the fried fish back in and simmer for 4 minutes more; sprinkle garam masala and serve with steamed rice or pulao. tip: kalia is the richer, special-occasion cousin of jhol — the onion-yogurt base and whole garam masala make it thicker and more festive.

recipes.title: Catla Fish Fry (Spiced Airfryer Catla)
recipes.search: catla fish fry (spiced airfryer catla) catla fish fry (spiced airfryer catla) airfryer – marinate 20 min + fry 200°c 14 min — serves 4 gluten-free • high-protein • everyday prep ahead: marinate the fish for at least 20 minutes before frying. ingredients 6 pieces catla fish 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1/2 tsp ajwain (carom seeds (ajwain)) 1 tbsp lemon juice 3 tbsp rice flour or semolina salt to taste oil spray method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 mix the fish pieces with ginger-garlic paste, chilli powder, turmeric, ajwain, lemon juice and salt; marinate for at least 20 minutes. 3 coat each piece in rice flour or semolina, pressing gently so it sticks. 4 spray generously with oil and arrange in a single layer in the airfryer basket. 5 air-fry at 200°c for 14 minutes, flipping halfway, until crisp and golden on both sides. 6 serve hot with onion rings and mint chutney. tip: catla has more bone than rohu around the belly — cutting it into steaks rather than fillets makes it easier to fry evenly and eat safely.

recipes.title: Bhapa Ilish (Steamed Hilsa in Mustard)
recipes.search: bhapa ilish (steamed hilsa in mustard) bhapa ilish (steamed hilsa in mustard) chef magic – steam auto 22 min — serves 4 gluten-free • bengali • high-protein prep ahead: marinate the fish in the mustard paste, turmeric and salt for at least 20 minutes before steaming. ingredients 4 hilsa fish pieces (or any firm fish) 3 tbsp mustard seeds (rai), ground to a paste 2 tbsp grated coconut 2 green chillies (hari mirch), slit 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 3 tbsp mustard oil (sarson ka tel) salt to taste method 1 mix mustard paste, coconut, turmeric, mustard oil and salt; coat the fish pieces and marinate 20 minutes. 2 place the marinated fish in a steel bowl that fits the steamer tray, topped with slit green chillies. 3 steam in chef magic (100°c steam, paddle off) for 22 minutes until the fish is opaque and fully cooked through. tip: traditionally served with plain steamed rice — the mustard gravy is the star of the dish.

recipes.title: Kerala-Style Fish Curry
recipes.search: kerala-style fish curry kerala-style fish curry chef magic – sauté + boil auto 22 min — serves 4 gluten-free • high-protein • kerala prep ahead: soak 2–3 pieces of kokum in warm water for 10 minutes if using, to soften before adding. ingredients 500g firm fish, cut into pieces 1 onion, sliced 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1.5 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 1/2 tsp turmeric (haldi) 1 cup coconut milk 2–3 pieces kokum (or 1 tbsp tamarind (imli) paste) 9 curry leaves (kadi patta) 2 tbsp coconut oil salt to taste method 1 add coconut oil and curry leaves to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook the sliced onion for 6 minutes until soft. 2 add ginger-garlic paste, chilli powder and turmeric; sauté 2 minutes. 3 add coconut milk, kokum and salt; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and simmer for 6 minutes. 4 gently add the fish pieces and simmer a further 8 minutes until just cooked through — avoid stirring hard so the fish stays intact.

recipes.title: Popcorn Shrimp
recipes.search: popcorn shrimp popcorn shrimp airfryer – fry 190°c 9 min — serves 4 high-protein • everyday ingredients 400g shrimp/prawns, peeled and deveined 1/2 cup cornflour 1/4 cup all-purpose flour 1/2 tsp paprika 1/2 tsp garlic powder salt to taste 1 egg, beaten 1 cup breadcrumbs oil spray method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 190°c for 4 minutes before adding the food to the basket. 2 pat the shrimp dry. mix the cornflour, flour, paprika, garlic powder and salt in a bowl. 3 toss the shrimp in the flour mix, dip in the beaten egg, then coat in breadcrumbs, pressing to help them stick. 4 spray lightly with oil and arrange in the basket in a single layer. 5 air-fry at 190°c for 7–9 minutes, shaking halfway, until golden and crisp — take care not to overcook, as shrimp turn rubbery quickly. tip: shrimp cook very fast — pull them the moment they turn opaque and the coating is golden, even if that's a minute earlier than the recipe states.

recipes.title: Popcorn Fish Bites
recipes.search: popcorn fish bites popcorn fish bites airfryer – fry 190°c 10 min — serves 4 high-protein • everyday ingredients 400g boneless white fish (basa or similar), cut into bite-sized pieces 1/2 cup cornflour 1/4 cup all-purpose flour 1/2 tsp paprika salt and black pepper to taste 1 egg, beaten 1 cup breadcrumbs oil spray method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 190°c for 4 minutes before adding the food to the basket. 2 pat the fish pieces dry. mix the cornflour, flour, paprika, salt and pepper in a bowl. 3 toss the fish in the flour mix, dip in the beaten egg, then coat in breadcrumbs. 4 spray lightly with oil and arrange in the basket in a single layer. 5 air-fry at 190°c for 8–10 minutes, shaking halfway, until golden and crisp and the fish flakes easily. tip: choose a firm white fish like basa or tilapia — flakier fish can fall apart during the toss-and-coat steps.

recipes.title: Fish Fingers (Fish Sticks)
recipes.search: fish fingers (fish sticks) fish fingers (fish sticks) airfryer – fry 190°c 12 min — serves 4 high-protein • everyday ingredients 500g boneless white fish, cut into finger-length strips 1/2 cup all-purpose flour 1/2 tsp salt 1/2 tsp black pepper 2 eggs, beaten 1.5 cups breadcrumbs oil spray lemon wedges and tartar sauce, to serve method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 190°c for 4 minutes before adding the food to the basket. 2 season the fish strips with salt and pepper. 3 dredge each strip in flour, dip in the beaten egg, then coat evenly in breadcrumbs, pressing to help them stick. 4 spray lightly with oil and arrange in the basket in a single layer. 5 air-fry at 190°c for 10–12 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp and the fish flakes easily. 6 serve hot with lemon wedges and tartar sauce. tip: freezing the coated fish fingers for 15 minutes before air-frying helps the crumb coating hold together better during cooking.

recipes.title: Chicken Manchurian (Dry)
recipes.search: chicken manchurian (dry) chicken manchurian (dry) airfryer (fry the chicken) → chef magic (toss in 200°c fry 16 min + toss 8 min sauce) — serves 4 high-protein • everyday • indo-chinese prep ahead: marinate the chicken pieces for at least 20 minutes for the best flavour. ingredients 500g boneless chicken, cubed 3 tbsp cornflour 2 tbsp maida (plain flour) 1 egg, beaten 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste), divided salt to taste oil spray 1 onion, cubed 1 capsicum, cubed 2 tbsp soy sauce 1 tbsp chilli sauce 1 tbsp tomato ketchup 1 tbsp vinegar 1/2 cup water mixed with 1 tsp cornflour spring onion greens to garnish method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 toss the chicken with cornflour, maida, beaten egg, half the ginger-garlic paste and salt; rest 20 minutes. 3 spray generously with oil and arrange in a single layer in the airfryer basket. 4 air-fry at 200°c for 16 minutes, shaking halfway, until golden and cooked through. 5 in chef magic, add a little oil; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook onion and capsicum with the remaining ginger-garlic paste for 4 minutes. 6 add soy sauce, chilli sauce, ketchup, vinegar and the cornflour-water mix; cook 2 minutes until glossy and thickened. 7 toss in the fried chicken just before serving so it stays crisp; garnish with spring onion. tip: the egg in the coating is what gives chicken manchurian its slightly richer, deeper-fried crust compared to the vegetarian

recipes.title: Chilli Chicken (Dry)
recipes.search: chilli chicken (dry) chilli chicken (dry) airfryer (fry the chicken) → chef magic (toss in 200°c fry 16 min + toss 8 min sauce) — serves 4 high-protein • everyday • indo-chinese prep ahead: marinate the chicken pieces for at least 20 minutes for the best flavour. ingredients 500g boneless chicken, cubed 3 tbsp cornflour 2 tbsp maida (plain flour) 1 egg, beaten 1 tbsp soy sauce, divided salt to taste oil spray 1 capsicum, cubed 1 onion, cubed 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1 tbsp chilli sauce 1 tbsp vinegar 2–3 green chillies (hari mirch), slit 1/2 cup water mixed with 1 tsp cornflour method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 toss the chicken with cornflour, maida, beaten egg, half the soy sauce and salt; rest 20 minutes. 3 spray generously with oil and arrange in a single layer in the airfryer basket. 4 air-fry at 200°c for 16 minutes, shaking halfway, until golden and cooked through. 5 in chef magic, add a little oil; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook capsicum, onion, ginger-garlic paste and green chillies for 4 minutes. 6 add remaining soy sauce, chilli sauce, vinegar and the cornflour-water mix; cook 2 minutes until thickened. 7 toss in the fried chicken just before serving; serve immediately while still crisp. tip: adjust the green chilli count to taste — restaurant versions typically run quite hot.

recipes.title: Chicken Hakka Noodles
recipes.search: chicken hakka noodles chicken hakka noodles chef magic – boil then sauté auto 22 min — serves 3 high-protein • everyday • indo-chinese prep ahead: rinse the boiled noodles under cold water and toss with a little oil to stop them sticking together. ingredients 200g hakka or thin noodles 200g boneless chicken, thinly sliced 1 cup thinly sliced mixed vegetables (cabbage, carrot, capsicum) 2 spring onions, sliced (whites and greens separated) 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 2 tbsp soy sauce 1 tsp vinegar 1 tsp chilli sauce (optional) 2 tbsp oil salt & pepper to taste method 1 add water and a pinch of salt to the jar; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and cook the noodles until just done, about 6 minutes; drain, rinse in cold water, and toss with a little oil. 2 add oil to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook the chicken with spring onion whites and ginger-garlic paste for 6 minutes until cooked through; remove and set aside. 3 add the mixed vegetables to the same jar and sauté for 5 minutes, keeping them crisp-tender. 4 return the chicken to the jar with the noodles, soy sauce, vinegar, chilli sauce and pepper; toss on sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) for 5 minutes until well combined. 5 garnish with spring onion greens and serve hot. tip: cook the chicken separately first and add it back at the end — this keeps it from overcooking while the noodles toss.

recipes.title: Chicken Manchow Soup
recipes.search: chicken manchow soup chicken manchow soup chef magic – sauté + boil auto 22 min — serves 4 high-protein • everyday • indo-chinese ingredients 200g boneless chicken, finely shredded or minced 1/2 cup finely chopped mixed vegetables (carrot, beans, cabbage) 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 2 tbsp soy sauce 1 tsp chilli sauce 1 tsp vinegar 4 cups chicken stock or water 2 tbsp cornflour, mixed with water, for the slurry 2 tbsp oil salt & pepper to taste fried noodles, spring onion greens, to garnish method 1 add oil to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook the ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute. 2 add the chicken and chopped vegetables; sauté for 6 minutes until the chicken is no longer pink. 3 add stock, soy sauce, chilli sauce and vinegar; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and simmer for 8 minutes. 4 stir in the cornflour slurry and cook a further 4 minutes until the soup turns glossy and slightly thickened. season with salt and pepper. 5 ladle into bowls and top with crispy fried noodles and spring onion greens. tip: shred or mince the chicken small — manchow soup pieces should be bite-sized, not chunky like a stew.

recipes.title: Honey Chilli Chicken
recipes.search: honey chilli chicken honey chilli chicken airfryer (fry the chicken) → chef magic (toss in 200°c fry 16 min + toss 6 min glaze) — serves 4 high-protein • everyday • indo-chinese prep ahead: marinate the chicken pieces for at least 20 minutes for the best flavour. ingredients 500g boneless chicken, cubed 3 tbsp cornflour 2 tbsp maida (plain flour) 1 egg, beaten salt to taste oil spray 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 1 capsicum, sliced 2 tbsp soy sauce 1 tbsp chilli sauce 2 tbsp honey 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds spring onion greens to garnish method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 toss the chicken with cornflour, maida, beaten egg and salt; rest 20 minutes. 3 spray generously with oil and arrange in a single layer in the airfryer basket. 4 air-fry at 200°c for 16 minutes, shaking halfway, until golden and cooked through. 5 in chef magic, add a little oil; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook ginger-garlic paste and capsicum for 2 minutes. 6 add soy sauce, chilli sauce and honey; simmer on sauté (speed 1–2, ~100–110°c) for 2 minutes until it turns into a light, sticky glaze. 7 toss in the crispy chicken just before serving; sprinkle with sesame seeds and spring onion. tip: toss right before serving — the honey glaze softens a crisp coating faster than a standard manchurian sauce does.

recipes.title: Dragon Chicken
recipes.search: dragon chicken dragon chicken airfryer (fry the chicken) → chef magic (toss in 200°c fry 16 min + toss 8 min sauce) — serves 4 high-protein • everyday • indo-chinese prep ahead: marinate the chicken pieces for at least 20 minutes for the best flavour. ingredients 500g boneless chicken, cut into thin strips 3 tbsp cornflour 2 tbsp maida (plain flour) 1 egg, beaten salt to taste oil spray 1 capsicum, julienned 1 onion, julienned 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (adrak-lehsun paste) 2 tbsp chilli-garlic (lehsun) sauce 1 tbsp tomato ketchup 1 tsp vinegar 1/2 tsp red chilli (lal mirch) flakes roasted cashews, roughly crushed, to garnish method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 toss the chicken strips with cornflour, maida, beaten egg and salt; rest 20 minutes. 3 spray with oil and arrange in a single layer in the airfryer basket. 4 air-fry at 200°c for 16 minutes, shaking halfway, until golden and cooked through. 5 in chef magic, add a little oil; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook capsicum, onion and ginger-garlic paste for 4 minutes, keeping the vegetables crisp. 6 add chilli-garlic sauce, ketchup, vinegar and chilli flakes; cook 2 minutes until glossy. 7 toss in the fried chicken just before serving; scatter with crushed cashews. tip: cutting the chicken into thin strips rather than cubes is what gives dragon chicken its characteristic long, crispy shred.

recipes.title: Chicken Fried Rice
recipes.search: chicken fried rice chicken fried rice chef magic – sauté auto 16 min — serves 3 high-protein • everyday • indo-chinese prep ahead: use a day-old cooked rice, chilled — fresh hot rice turns mushy when stir-fried. ingredients 3 cups cooked basmati rice, chilled 200g boneless chicken, finely diced 1 egg, lightly beaten 1/2 cup mixed vegetables (carrot, beans, capsicum), finely diced 2 spring onions, chopped, greens and whites separated 2 cloves garlic (lehsun), minced 2 tbsp soy sauce 1 tsp vinegar 1/2 tsp white pepper (safed mirch) 2 tbsp oil salt to taste method 1 in chef magic, add 1 tbsp oil; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook the chicken for 6 minutes until cooked through. remove and set aside. 2 add the remaining oil, garlic and spring onion whites; sauté for 1 minute. 3 add the mixed vegetables and stir-fry for 3 minutes until just tender-crisp. 4 push everything to one side, pour in the beaten egg and scramble for 1 minute, then mix through. 5 add the rice, breaking up any clumps, along with the cooked chicken, soy sauce, vinegar, white pepper and salt; toss on sauté for 4 minutes until well combined and lightly charred in spots. 6 garnish with spring onion greens and serve hot. tip: keep the flame (sauté speed) high and toss quickly — fried rice should sizzle, not steam.

recipes.title: Chicken Noodle Soup (Everyday)
recipes.search: chicken noodle soup (everyday) chicken noodle soup (everyday) chef magic – sauté + boil auto 24 min — serves 4 high-protein • everyday ingredients 200g boneless chicken, shredded or thinly sliced 100g noodles (any thin noodles) 1 carrot, julienned 1/2 cup shredded cabbage 2 cloves garlic (lehsun), minced 1 inch ginger (adrak), julienned 4 cups chicken or vegetable stock 1 tbsp soy sauce 1 tsp oil salt and pepper to taste spring onion greens to garnish method 1 in chef magic, add oil; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and sauté garlic and ginger for 1 minute until fragrant. 2 add the chicken and cook for 4 minutes until it changes colour. 3 add the stock and soy sauce; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and bring to a simmer for 6 minutes. 4 add the noodles, carrot and cabbage; continue on boil for 6 minutes until the noodles are just tender. 5 season with salt and pepper, and garnish with spring onion greens before serving hot. tip: a simple, everyday soup — swap in whatever vegetables you have on hand, it's forgiving that way.

recipes.title: Chicken Parmesan
recipes.search: chicken parmesan chicken parmesan airfryer (fry) then (bake) 190°c fry 14 min + bake 5 min — serves 3 high-protein • everyday • italian ingredients 3 boneless chicken breasts, flattened 1/2 cup flour 2 eggs, beaten 1 cup breadcrumbs mixed with 1/4 cup grated parmesan 1 cup marinara sauce 1 cup shredded mozzarella salt & pepper to taste oil spray method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 190°c for 4 minutes before adding the food to the basket. 2 season chicken with salt and pepper; coat in flour, then egg, then the breadcrumb-parmesan mix. 3 spray the chicken with oil and arrange in the basket. 4 air-fry at 190°c for 14 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden and cooked through. 5 top each piece with marinara sauce and mozzarella; bake a further 5 minutes at 190°c until the cheese melts.

recipes.title: Chicken Alfredo Pasta
recipes.search: chicken alfredo pasta chicken alfredo pasta airfryer (grill chicken) → chef magic (boil pasta + make sauce) 190°c grill 14 min + boil 11 min + sauce 8 min — serves 3 high-protein • everyday • italian prep ahead: slice the chicken only after it rests for a couple of minutes off the heat — it stays juicier and slices more cleanly. ingredients 2 boneless chicken breasts 1 tbsp olive oil, plus extra for the pasta water 1/2 tsp black pepper salt to taste 250g fettuccine or penne 2 tbsp butter 3 cloves garlic, finely chopped 1 cup fresh cream 1/2 cup grated parmesan, plus extra to serve 1/4 tsp nutmeg (optional) chopped parsley, to garnish method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 190°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 rub the chicken breasts with olive oil, black pepper and salt; air-fry at 190°c for 14 minutes, flipping halfway, until cooked through. rest, then slice. 3 meanwhile, add water and a pinch of salt to the chef magic jar; select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and cook the pasta until al dente, about 11 minutes; drain and set aside. 4 add butter to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook the garlic for 1 minute until fragrant, not browned. 5 add the cream, parmesan and nutmeg if using; simmer on sauté (speed 1–2, ~100–110°c) for 6 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly. 6 add the drained pasta to the sauce and toss for 2 minutes until well coated. top with the sliced chicken, extra parmesan and parsley; serve hot. tip: the sauce will look thin at first but keeps thickening off the heat as the parmesan sets — don't over-reduce it in the jar.

recipes.title: French Onion Soup
recipes.search: french onion soup french onion soup chef magic (caramelise & simmer) → airfryer 200°c 42 min total (melt cheese topping) — serves 4 vegetarian • french prep ahead: slice onions thinly and evenly — this helps them caramelise at the same rate. ingredients 4 large onions, thinly sliced 3 tbsp butter 1 tsp sugar 4 cups mutton or vegetable stock 1 tbsp flour 4 slices baguette 1 cup grated gruyère or mozzarella salt & pepper to taste method 1 preheat: when you reach the airfryer step, preheat it to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 add butter to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook the sliced onions with sugar for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deep golden-brown and caramelised. 3 stir in flour and cook 2 minutes, then add stock, salt and pepper. 4 select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and simmer for 10 minutes. 5 ladle into oven-safe bowls, top with baguette slices and cheese, then air-fry at 200°c for 5 minutes until the cheese melts and bubbles.

recipes.title: Chicken Souvlaki Skewers
recipes.search: chicken souvlaki skewers chicken souvlaki skewers airfryer – grill 200°c 15 min — serves 4 gluten-free • high-protein • mediterranean • everyday prep ahead: marinate the chicken for at least 30 minutes (up to overnight) for the best flavour. ingredients 500g boneless chicken, cubed 3 tbsp olive oil 2 tbsp lemon juice 2 cloves garlic, minced 1 tbsp dried oregano salt & pepper to taste method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food to the basket. 2 mix olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper; marinate the chicken for at least 30 minutes. 3 skewer or arrange the chicken in the basket. 4 grill at 200°c for 15 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges and cooked through. 5 serve with pita, tzatziki and salad.

recipes.title: One-Pot Chicken Paella
recipes.search: one-pot chicken paella one-pot chicken paella chef magic – sauté + boil auto 34 min — serves 4 gluten-free • high-protein • spanish ingredients 500g chicken thighs, cubed 1.5 cups short-grain rice 1 onion, chopped 1 bell pepper, chopped 2 tomatoes, chopped 1/2 cup peas a few saffron strands in warm water 1 tsp smoked paprika 3 cups chicken stock 3 tbsp olive oil salt & pepper to taste lemon wedges to serve method 1 add olive oil to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and brown the chicken for 8 minutes; remove and set aside. 2 in the same jar, cook onion and bell pepper for 5 minutes, then add tomatoes and smoked paprika, cooking 3 minutes. 3 add rice, stock, saffron water, salt and pepper, and return the chicken to the jar. 4 select boil (speed 1–2, 100°c) and cook for 16 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed; stir in peas for the last 2 minutes. serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.title: Crispy Airfryer Fish and Chips
recipes.search: crispy airfryer fish and chips crispy airfryer fish and chips airfryer – fry 200°c 20 min — serves 3 high-protein • british • everyday ingredients 3 firm white fish fillets 1/2 cup flour 1 egg, beaten 1 cup panko breadcrumbs 3 potatoes, cut into thick chips 2 tbsp oil salt & pepper to taste malt vinegar to serve method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food to the basket. 2 toss the potato chips with oil and salt; air-fry the chips at 200°c for 10 minutes. 3 meanwhile, coat fish fillets in flour, then beaten egg, then panko breadcrumbs. 4 push the chips to one side of the basket, spray the fish with oil, and add to the basket. 5 air-fry both together at 200°c for a further 10 minutes, until fish is golden and flakes easily and chips are crisp. serve with malt vinegar.

recipes.title: Shepherd’s Pie
recipes.search: shepherd’s pie shepherd’s pie chef magic (cook filling & mash) → airfryer 190°c sauté 18 min + bake 20 min (bake topping) — serves 4 gluten-free • high-protein • british ingredients 500g minced lamb or mutton 1 onion, chopped 1 carrot, diced 1/2 cup peas 2 tbsp tomato paste 1 cup stock 1 tbsp worcestershire sauce (optional) 4 potatoes, boiled & mashed 2 tbsp butter 2 tbsp milk salt & pepper to taste method 1 preheat: when you reach the airfryer step, preheat it to 190°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 add a little oil to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–160°c) and cook the onion and carrot for 6 minutes, then add the minced meat and brown for 8 minutes. 3 stir in tomato paste, stock and worcestershire sauce; simmer on sauté (speed 1–2, ~100–110°c) for 8 minutes until thick, then fold in peas. 4 separately, mash boiled potatoes with butter, milk, salt and pepper until smooth. 5 spread the meat filling in an oven-safe dish, top with mashed potato, and bake in the airfryer at 190°c for 20 minutes until the top is golden.

recipes.title: Chicken Burger (Crispy Chicken Patty Burger)
recipes.search: chicken burger (crispy chicken patty burger) chicken burger (crispy chicken patty burger) airfryer – fry 200°c 18 min — serves 4 high-protein • everyday • continental prep ahead: chill the shaped patties for at least 30 minutes (or freeze for 10 minutes) before air-frying so they hold together and stay juicy. ingredients 500g boneless chicken, minced 1/2 cup breadcrumbs, plus extra for coating 1 egg 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste 1/2 tsp black pepper 1/2 tsp red chilli powder 1 tbsp chopped coriander salt to taste oil spray 4 burger buns butter, for toasting the buns lettuce leaves, tomato & onion slices mayonnaise & ketchup, to serve 4 cheese slices (optional) method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 in a bowl, combine minced chicken, breadcrumbs, egg, ginger-garlic paste, black pepper, chilli powder, coriander and salt; mix until just combined (don't overwork it). 3 shape into 4 patties and chill for at least 30 minutes. 4 coat each patty lightly in extra breadcrumbs and spray generously with oil. 5 air-fry at 200°c for 18 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden, crisp and cooked through. 6 in the last 2 minutes, halve the buns and toast lightly with a little butter; melt a cheese slice onto each patty if using. 7 assemble: bun base, sauces, lettuce, tomato, onion, the patty, and the bun top. serve hot. tip: press a small dimple into the centre of each patty before cooking — chicken patties puff up in the middle as they cook, and the dimple keeps them flat.

recipes.title: Korean Fried Chicken (Yangnyeom Chicken)
recipes.search: korean fried chicken (yangnyeom chicken) korean fried chicken (yangnyeom chicken) airfryer + chef magic – fry 20 min + sauce 2 min — serves 4 high-protein • korean • everyday ingredients 500g boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces 1/2 cup cornflour 1/4 cup all-purpose flour 1 egg, beaten salt and black pepper to taste 4 tbsp gochujang 2 tbsp honey 2 tbsp soy sauce 1 tbsp rice vinegar 2 cloves garlic, minced 1 tsp sesame oil toasted sesame seeds, to garnish method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food to the basket. 2 season the chicken with salt and pepper. dip each piece in the beaten egg, then dredge in a mix of cornflour and flour, pressing to coat well. 3 arrange the chicken in the basket in a single layer, spraying lightly with oil. 4 air-fry at 200°c for 18–20 minutes, shaking halfway, until deeply golden and crisp. 5 while the chicken cooks, combine the gochujang, honey, soy sauce, rice vinegar, garlic and sesame oil in the jar; select sauté (speed 1, ~90–100°c) and warm for 2 minutes until glossy. 6 toss the hot chicken in the sauce until well coated, garnish with sesame seeds, and serve immediately. tip: for extra-crackly restaurant-style crunch, air-fry the chicken once, let it rest for 5 minutes, then air-fry again for 5 minutes before saucing — the "double-fry" effect works in the airfryer too.

recipes.title: Korean Gochujang Chicken Wings
recipes.search: korean gochujang chicken wings korean gochujang chicken wings airfryer + chef magic – fry 25 min + sauce 2 min — serves 4 high-protein • korean • everyday ingredients 1 kg chicken wings 1 tbsp baking powder (for extra crispness) salt to taste 3 tbsp gochujang 2 tbsp honey 1 tbsp soy sauce 1 tbsp rice vinegar 2 cloves garlic, minced 1 tsp sesame oil toasted sesame seeds and sliced spring onion, to garnish method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food to the basket. 2 pat the wings completely dry, then toss with the baking powder and salt. 3 arrange in the basket in a single layer, without overcrowding. 4 air-fry at 200°c for 22–25 minutes, shaking every 8 minutes, until deeply golden and crisp. 5 meanwhile, combine the gochujang, honey, soy sauce, rice vinegar, garlic and sesame oil in the jar; select sauté (speed 1, ~90–100°c) and warm for 2 minutes. 6 toss the hot wings in the sauce, garnish with sesame seeds and spring onion, and serve immediately. tip: the baking powder coating (not baking soda) is the secret to shatter-crisp wing skin in the airfryer, without any deep frying.

recipes.title: Korean Chicken Bulgogi
recipes.search: korean chicken bulgogi korean chicken bulgogi chef magic (marinade) → airfryer 200°c marinate 1 hr + fry 16 min — serves 4 high-protein • korean • everyday ingredients 600g boneless chicken thighs, thinly sliced 1/2 cup soy sauce 3 tbsp brown sugar 2 tbsp sesame oil 1 asian pear or apple, grated 4 cloves garlic, minced 1 tbsp grated ginger 1 onion, sliced 2 spring onions, cut into batons toasted sesame seeds, to garnish method 1 in the jar, combine the soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, grated pear, garlic and ginger; select whisk/blend (speed 4–6) and blend into a smooth marinade. 2 toss the chicken and onion in the marinade, cover, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, or overnight for best flavour. 3 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food to the basket. 4 arrange the marinated chicken and onion in the basket in a single layer. 5 air-fry at 200°c for 14–16 minutes, shaking halfway, until caramelised and cooked through. 6 garnish with spring onions and sesame seeds; serve with steamed rice and lettuce wraps. tip: slicing the chicken thinly, against the grain, helps it soak up the marinade faster and cook quickly and evenly.

recipes.title: Korean Corn Dogs
recipes.search: korean corn dogs korean corn dogs airfryer – fry 190°c 14 min — serves 4 high-protein • korean • everyday ingredients 4 chicken sausages 4 wooden skewers 1 cup all-purpose flour 2 tbsp sugar 1 tsp baking powder 1/2 tsp salt 1 egg 3/4 cup milk 1 cup breadcrumbs or crushed cornflakes, for coating ketchup and mustard, to serve method 1 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 190°c for 4 minutes before adding the food to the basket. 2 pat the sausages dry and skewer each one lengthwise. 3 whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, egg and milk into a smooth, thick batter. 4 dip each skewered sausage in the batter to coat evenly, then roll in the breadcrumbs, pressing to help them stick. 5 spray lightly with oil and arrange in the basket, spaced apart. 6 air-fry at 190°c for 12–14 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp. serve hot with ketchup and mustard. tip: popular street-food versions roll the coated corn dog in sugar right after frying for a sweet-savoury crust — try it if you have a sweet tooth.

recipes.title: Chicken Shawarma (Airfryer)
recipes.search: chicken shawarma (airfryer) chicken shawarma (airfryer) chef magic (mix marinade) → airfryer 200°c marinate 30 min + grill 16 min — serves 4 high-protein • everyday prep ahead: marinate the chicken for at least 30 minutes before grilling. ingredients 500g boneless chicken thighs, sliced 2 tbsp yogurt 1 tbsp lemon juice 1 tbsp oil 1 tsp cumin powder (jeera powder) 1 tsp coriander powder (dhania powder) 1/2 tsp paprika 1/4 tsp cinnamon (dalchini) powder 2 cloves garlic (lehsun), minced salt to taste pita or flatbread, sliced onion, tomato and garlic (lehsun) sauce to serve method 1 preheat: when you reach the airfryer step, preheat it to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 in chef magic, mix the yogurt, lemon juice, oil, cumin, coriander, paprika, cinnamon, garlic and salt into a marinade. 3 coat the chicken slices well and rest for at least 30 minutes. 4 arrange the chicken in a single layer in the airfryer basket. 5 grill at 200°c for 16 minutes, tossing halfway, until charred at the edges and cooked through. 6 pile into warm pita or flatbread with sliced onion, tomato and garlic sauce. tip: slicing the chicken thin before marinating means it grills fast and shreds easily, just like a spit-roasted shawarma.

recipes.title: Homemade Paneer (Fresh Cottage Cheese)
recipes.search: homemade paneer (fresh cottage cheese) homemade paneer (fresh cottage cheese) chef magic – boil + sauté 15 min + draining 20 min — makes ~250g gluten-free • vegetarian • high-protein • homemade ingredients 1.5 litres full-fat milk 3 tbsp lemon juice or vinegar, mixed with 3 tbsp water ice cubes, for shocking (optional) method 1 add the milk to the jar; select boil (speed 1, 100°c) and bring to a gentle boil, stirring occasionally to stop it catching. 2 once boiling, switch to sauté (speed 1, ~90°c) and slowly add the lemon juice-water mixture, stirring gently until the milk curdles and clear whey separates. 3 turn off and let it sit for 2 minutes, then pour through a muslin-lined strainer, collecting the whey separately. 4 rinse the paneer briefly under cold water to remove any sour taste, then gather the muslin cloth and gently squeeze out the excess water. 5 tie the cloth and hang for 20 minutes to drain, or press under a heavy weight for 30 minutes for firmer paneer. 6 unwrap, cut into cubes, and use fresh, or refrigerate for up to 3 days. tip: save the leftover whey — it's great for kneading dough or stirring into dal for extra nutrition.

recipes.title: Homemade Ghee (Clarified Butter)
recipes.search: homemade ghee (clarified butter) homemade ghee (clarified butter) chef magic – sauté 18 min — makes ~400ml gluten-free • vegetarian • homemade ingredients 500g unsalted butter (or fresh malai/cream collected over a few days) method 1 add the butter to the jar; select sauté (speed 1–2, ~110–120°c) and let it melt completely. 2 continue cooking, stirring occasionally, as it foams and the milk solids separate and sink, slowly turning golden — this takes about 15–18 minutes. 3 once the ghee turns clear golden and smells nutty, with browned solids settled at the bottom, turn off immediately to avoid burning. 4 let cool for 5 minutes, then strain through a fine muslin cloth or fine sieve into a clean, dry glass jar. 5 cool completely before sealing; store at room temperature for up to 3 months. tip: don't throw out the browned milk solids left in the strainer — stir them into hot rice or dal for a delicious treat.

recipes.title: Homemade White Butter (Makkhan)
recipes.search: homemade white butter (makkhan) homemade white butter (makkhan) chef magic – whisk/blend 8 min — makes ~150g gluten-free • vegetarian • homemade ingredients 2 cups fresh cream (malai), chilled, or store-bought heavy cream 1/2 cup ice-cold water ice cubes method 1 add the chilled cream to the jar; select whisk/blend (speed 6–8) and whip for 3–4 minutes until it thickens. 2 continue whisking — the mixture will pass through a whipped-cream stage and then separate into solid butter grains and thin buttermilk (chaas), taking another 4–5 minutes. 3 add a splash of the ice-cold water and pulse briefly to help the butter grains clump together. 4 strain off the buttermilk (save it — it's delicious!), then gather the butter and rinse under cold water, kneading gently to remove any remaining buttermilk. 5 shape into a block, wrap, and refrigerate. use fresh within a week, or clarify into ghee for longer storage. tip: keep everything cold — the cream, the bowl, even the water — so the butter forms quickly and cleanly.

recipes.title: Hung Curd (Chakka Dahi)
recipes.search: hung curd (chakka dahi) hung curd (chakka dahi) no-cook – hang/strain 4–6 hrs — makes ~250g gluten-free • vegetarian • high-protein • no-cook finish • homemade ingredients 500g fresh curd/yogurt (thick, homemade or store-bought) method 1 line a strainer or colander with a clean muslin cloth and set it over a bowl. 2 pour the curd into the cloth-lined strainer. 3 gather the corners of the cloth and tie into a bundle; hang over the bowl (or place a light weight on top) and refrigerate for 4–6 hours, or overnight for very thick hung curd. 4 discard or reserve the collected whey — it's great stirred into smoothies or dough. 5 transfer the thick hung curd to a bowl and use for dips, desserts, or as a substitute for cream. tip: the longer you hang it, the thicker it gets — go overnight for a greek-yogurt-style consistency perfect for dips like tzatziki.

recipes.title: Homemade Khoya (Mawa)
recipes.search: homemade khoya (mawa) homemade khoya (mawa) chef magic – boil + sauté 45 min — makes ~200g gluten-free • vegetarian • homemade ingredients 1 litre full-fat milk method 1 add the milk to the jar; select boil (speed 1, 100°c) and bring to a boil. 2 once boiling, switch to sauté (speed 1–2, ~110–120°c) and simmer, stirring frequently, as the milk reduces. 3 continue simmering and stirring for 35–40 minutes as the milk thickens into a soft, grainy mass, scraping down the sides regularly to stop it sticking. 4 once the mixture pulls away from the sides and forms a soft, dough-like mass, turn off and let it cool slightly. 5 use immediately in sweets, or cool completely and refrigerate for up to a week. tip: stir constantly in the final 10 minutes — khoya can catch and burn quickly once most of the moisture has evaporated.

recipes.title: Homemade Mozzarella (Stretchy Fresh Cheese)
recipes.search: homemade mozzarella (stretchy fresh cheese) homemade mozzarella (stretchy fresh cheese) chef magic – sauté 20 min + stretch 10 min — makes ~250g gluten-free • vegetarian • homemade ingredients 2 litres whole milk (not ultra-pasteurised) 1.5 tsp citric acid, dissolved in 1/4 cup cool water 1/4 tablet rennet, dissolved in 1/4 cup cool water (or 1/4 tsp liquid rennet) 1 tsp salt extra water, for stretching (heated separately) method 1 add the milk to the jar; select sauté (speed 1, ~30–35°c) and warm gently. add the citric acid solution, stirring to combine. 2 continue warming to about 32°c, then add the rennet solution and stir gently for 30 seconds. turn off and let it sit undisturbed for 5 minutes until it sets into a custard-like curd. 3 cut the curd into 2cm cubes with a knife. select sauté (speed 1, ~40°c) and gently heat for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the curds firm up and separate further from the whey. 4 scoop out the curds with a slotted spoon into a bowl, pressing gently to remove excess whey. 5 heat a separate bowl of water to just below boiling. submerge the curd ball in the hot water for 30 seconds, then remove and knead/stretch it like taffy, folding and pulling until smooth and glossy, dipping back into the hot water as needed to keep it pliable. 6 add the salt, shape into a ball, and place in ice water to firm up. store refrigerated in its whey for up to a week. tip: mozzarella needs true dairy (not ultra-pasteurised) milk to set properly — check the carton before you start.

recipes.title: Homemade Cream Cheese
recipes.search: homemade cream cheese homemade cream cheese chef magic – boil + whisk/blend 20 min + draining 1 hr — makes ~300g gluten-free • vegetarian • homemade ingredients 1 litre full-fat milk 500ml fresh cream 3 tbsp lemon juice or white vinegar 1/4 tsp salt method 1 add the milk and cream to the jar; select boil (speed 1, 100°c) and bring to a gentle boil, stirring occasionally. 2 once boiling, reduce to sauté (speed 1, ~90°c) and slowly add the lemon juice, stirring gently until it curdles and clear whey separates. 3 turn off and let it sit for 2 minutes, then pour through a fine muslin-lined strainer. 4 rinse briefly under cold water, then tie the cloth and hang to drain for 1 hour. 5 transfer the drained curds to chef magic; select whisk/blend (speed 6–8) with the salt, blending for 1–2 minutes until completely smooth and spreadable, scraping down the sides as needed. 6 transfer to an airtight container and refrigerate for up to a week. tip: for a tangier, deli-style cream cheese, let the curds drain for a full 2 hours before blending.

recipes.title: Classic Eggless Mayonnaise
recipes.search: classic eggless mayonnaise classic eggless mayonnaise chef magic – whisk/blend 4 min — makes ~1.5 cups gluten-free • vegetarian • eggless • homemade ingredients 1/2 cup full-fat milk, cold 1 cup neutral oil (sunflower or vegetable) 1 tbsp lemon juice or white vinegar 1/2 tsp mustard powder (optional) 1/2 tsp sugar salt to taste method 1 add the cold milk to the jar; select whisk/blend (speed 8–10) and blend for 20 seconds. 2 with the machine running on whisk/blend (speed 8–10), slowly drizzle in the oil in a thin, steady stream over 2–3 minutes until the mixture thickens and emulsifies into a mayonnaise-like consistency. 3 add the lemon juice, mustard powder, sugar and salt; blend for another 15 seconds to combine. 4 taste and adjust salt or lemon juice as needed. transfer to a clean jar and refrigerate. tip: everything works best cold — chilled milk with room-temperature oil added slowly is the secret to a mayo that doesn't split.

recipes.title: Garlic Mayo (Aioli-Style)
recipes.search: garlic mayo (aioli-style) garlic mayo (aioli-style) no-cook – mix + rest 30 min — makes ~1 cup gluten-free • vegetarian • no-cook finish • homemade ingredients 1 cup classic eggless mayonnaise (or store-bought) 4 cloves garlic (lehsun), finely grated or crushed 1 tsp lemon juice 1/2 tsp black pepper (kali mirch) salt to taste method 1 in a bowl, combine the mayonnaise with the grated garlic. 2 stir in the lemon juice, black pepper and salt, mixing until fully combined. 3 cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to let the garlic flavour infuse before serving. tip: for a milder, sweeter garlic flavour, lightly sauté the garlic in a teaspoon of oil for 1 minute before stirring it in.

recipes.title: Homemade Tomato Ketchup
recipes.search: homemade tomato ketchup homemade tomato ketchup chef magic – boil + blend + sauté 45 min — makes ~500ml gluten-free • vegetarian • homemade ingredients 1 kg ripe tomatoes, chopped 1 onion, chopped 3 cloves garlic (lehsun) 1-inch ginger (adrak), chopped 1/2 cup sugar 1/3 cup vinegar 1 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 1/2 tsp cinnamon (dalchini) powder 1/4 tsp cloves (laung) powder salt to taste method 1 add the tomatoes, onion, garlic and ginger to the jar; select boil (speed 1, 100°c) and cook for 15 minutes until the tomatoes break down completely. 2 select whisk/blend (speed 8–10) and blend until completely smooth, then pass through a sieve to remove skins and seeds if a very smooth ketchup is desired (optional). 3 return the puree to the jar; select sauté (speed 1–2, ~110–130°c) and add the sugar, vinegar, chilli powder, cinnamon, clove powder and salt. 4 simmer, stirring occasionally, for 25–30 minutes until thickened to a ketchup-like consistency that coats the back of a spoon. 5 cool completely, then bottle in a clean, sterilised jar. refrigerate for up to a month. tip: ketchup thickens further as it cools, so stop simmering when it's still slightly thinner than you want the final result.

recipes.title: White Sauce (Béchamel)
recipes.search: white sauce (béchamel) white sauce (béchamel) chef magic – sauté 10 min — makes ~2 cups vegetarian • homemade ingredients 2 tbsp butter 2 tbsp all-purpose flour (maida) 2 cups milk, warmed 1/4 tsp nutmeg (jaiphal), grated salt and black pepper (kali mirch) to taste method 1 add the butter to the jar; select sauté (speed 1–2, ~110–120°c) and melt completely. 2 add the flour and whisk continuously for 2 minutes to cook out the raw taste, without letting it brown. 3 gradually add the warm milk in small splashes, whisking constantly on sauté (speed 1–2) to avoid lumps, until fully incorporated. 4 continue cooking, stirring constantly, for 5–6 minutes until the sauce thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon. 5 stir in the nutmeg, salt and pepper. use immediately in bakes, pastas or gratins. tip: warming the milk before adding it prevents lumps and speeds up thickening — cold milk is the most common cause of a lumpy white sauce.

recipes.title: Pizza & Pasta Sauce (Marinara)
recipes.search: pizza & pasta sauce (marinara) pizza & pasta sauce (marinara) chef magic – sauté + boil 30 min — makes ~500ml gluten-free • vegetarian • homemade ingredients 1 kg ripe tomatoes, roughly chopped (or 2 cans crushed tomatoes) 4 cloves garlic (lehsun), sliced 2 tbsp olive oil 1 tsp dried oregano 1/2 tsp red chilli flakes (lal mirch flakes) 1 tsp sugar salt to taste a few fresh basil leaves (optional) method 1 add the olive oil and garlic to the jar; select sauté (speed 1–2, ~120–140°c) and cook for 1–2 minutes until fragrant, without browning. 2 add the tomatoes, oregano, chilli flakes, sugar and salt; select boil (speed 1, 100°c) and bring to a simmer. 3 reduce to sauté (speed 1, ~100–110°c) and simmer for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened and the raw tomato taste has cooked out. 4 for a smooth sauce, select whisk/blend (speed 6–8) and blend briefly to the desired consistency; for a chunky sauce, leave as is. 5 stir in fresh basil leaves if using, just before serving. tip: a pinch of sugar balances the acidity of the tomatoes — taste and adjust at the end rather than adding it all upfront.

recipes.title: Peri Peri Sauce
recipes.search: peri peri sauce peri peri sauce chef magic – whisk/blend 5 min — makes ~1 cup gluten-free • vegetarian • homemade ingredients 4–5 dried red chillies (lal mirch), soaked in warm water 2 fresh red chillies (lal mirch) 4 cloves garlic (lehsun) 1 tbsp paprika 1 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 2 tbsp lemon juice 2 tbsp vinegar 3 tbsp olive oil 1 tsp sugar salt to taste method 1 drain the soaked dried chillies and add to the jar along with the fresh chillies, garlic, paprika, chilli powder, lemon juice, vinegar, sugar and salt. 2 select whisk/blend (speed 8–10) and blend until smooth, scraping down the sides as needed. 3 with the machine running on whisk/blend (speed 6–8), slowly drizzle in the olive oil to emulsify the sauce. 4 transfer to a clean bottle and refrigerate for up to 2 weeks; the flavour deepens after a day. tip: this sauce doubles as a fantastic marinade — toss chicken or paneer in it for at least an hour before air-frying.

recipes.title: Schezwan Sauce
recipes.search: schezwan sauce schezwan sauce chef magic – blend + sauté 15 min — makes ~1 cup vegetarian • homemade • indo-chinese ingredients 15–20 dried red chillies (lal mirch), soaked in hot water for 20 minutes 8 cloves garlic (lehsun), chopped 1-inch ginger (adrak), chopped 3 tbsp oil 2 tbsp tomato ketchup 1 tbsp soy sauce 1 tbsp vinegar 1 tsp sugar salt to taste method 1 drain the soaked chillies and add to the jar with a splash of water; select whisk/blend (speed 8–10) and blend into a smooth paste. 2 add the oil, garlic and ginger to the jar; select sauté (speed 2–4, ~130–150°c) and cook for 2 minutes until fragrant. 3 add the chilli paste and cook, stirring frequently, for 6–8 minutes until the oil separates and the raw smell disappears. 4 stir in the ketchup, soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and salt; simmer on sauté (speed 1–2) for 3–4 minutes until glossy and thickened. 5 cool and bottle; refrigerate for up to 3 weeks. tip: this is the base for almost every indo-chinese dry dish in this book — stir a spoonful into fried rice or noodles for an instant flavour boost.

recipes.title: BBQ Sauce
recipes.search: bbq sauce bbq sauce chef magic – sauté 12 min — makes ~1.5 cups vegetarian • homemade ingredients 1 cup tomato ketchup 2 tbsp brown sugar or jaggery (gud) 2 tbsp vinegar 1 tbsp worcestershire sauce (optional) 1 tsp smoked paprika 1/2 tsp garlic powder 1/2 tsp onion powder 1/4 tsp black pepper (kali mirch) salt to taste method 1 add all the ingredients to the jar; select sauté (speed 1–2, ~100–110°c) and stir to combine. 2 simmer, stirring occasionally, for 8–10 minutes until slightly thickened and glossy. 3 cool completely before bottling; refrigerate for up to 3 weeks. tip: brush this on chicken or paneer skewers in the last 3–4 minutes of air-frying for a sticky, caramelised glaze without burning the sugars.

recipes.title: Cheese Sauce (for Mac & Cheese, Nachos)
