recipes.search: cheese sauce (for mac & cheese, nachos) cheese sauce (for mac & cheese, nachos) chef magic – sauté 10 min — makes ~2 cups vegetarian • homemade ingredients 2 tbsp butter 2 tbsp all-purpose flour (maida) 1.5 cups milk, warmed 1.5 cups grated cheddar cheese 1/4 tsp mustard powder a pinch of nutmeg (jaiphal) salt and black pepper (kali mirch) to taste method 1 add the butter to the jar; select sauté (speed 1–2, ~110–120°c) and melt completely. 2 add the flour and whisk continuously for 2 minutes without browning. 3 gradually whisk in the warm milk, a little at a time, until smooth and fully incorporated. 4 cook, stirring constantly, for 4–5 minutes until thickened. 5 turn off the heat and stir in the grated cheese, mustard powder, nutmeg, salt and pepper until melted and smooth. tip: take the sauce off the heat before adding the cheese — direct high heat can make it grainy instead of silky.

recipes.title: Sweet Tamarind Chutney (Meethi Chutney)
recipes.search: sweet tamarind chutney (meethi chutney) sweet tamarind chutney (meethi chutney) chef magic – sauté 16 min — makes ~1.5 cups gluten-free • vegetarian • homemade ingredients 200g tamarind (imli), soaked in 1.5 cups hot water for 30 minutes 150g jaggery (gud), grated 1 tsp roasted cumin (jeera) powder 1/2 tsp red chilli powder (lal mirch powder) 1/2 tsp dry ginger (saunth) powder 1/4 tsp black salt salt to taste method 1 squeeze the soaked tamarind well to extract the pulp, then strain through a sieve to remove fibres and seeds; discard the solids. 2 add the tamarind pulp and jaggery to the jar; select sauté (speed 1–2, ~110–120°c) and simmer for 10–12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the jaggery dissolves and the mixture thickens slightly. 3 stir in the roasted cumin powder, chilli powder, dry ginger powder, black salt and salt; simmer for another 3–4 minutes. 4 cool completely — the chutney will thicken further as it cools. bottle and refrigerate for up to a month. tip: this chutney freezes well in an ice cube tray — pop out a cube whenever a recipe calls for a spoonful.

recipes.title: Chapati / Roti Dough
recipes.search: chapati / roti dough chapati / roti dough chef magic – knead — 6 min makes 9 rotis ingredients 2 cups whole wheat flour 3/4 cup water (approx.) 1/2 tsp salt 1 tsp oil method 1 add flour, salt and oil to the jar. 2 select knead (speed 2–3, no heat) and gradually pour in water through the lid opening while it mixes. 3 knead until a smooth, soft dough forms. 4 rest the dough 15 minutes before rolling and cooking rotis on a tawa.

recipes.title: Whole Wheat Pizza, Dough to Bake
recipes.search: whole wheat pizza, dough to bake whole wheat pizza, dough to bake chef magic (knead) → airfryer (bake) 200°c — knead 5 min + rest 1 hr + bake 11 min — makes 2 pizzas ingredients 2 cups whole wheat flour 1 tsp instant yeast 1 tsp sugar 3/4 cup warm water (105–110°f / 40–43°c) 2 tbsp oil 1/2 tsp salt pizza sauce, cheese & toppings of choice method 1 preheat: when you reach the airfryer step, preheat it to 200°c for 4 minutes before adding the food. 2 in chef magic, dissolve yeast and sugar in warm water heated to 105–110°f (40–43°c) — warm to the touch, not hot; anything above 120°f (49°c) will kill the yeast; let sit 5–10 minutes until frothy. 3 add flour, oil and salt to the jar with the yeast mixture; select knead (speed 2–3, no heat) until a smooth, elastic dough forms. 4 cover and let the dough rise for about 1 hour, until doubled. 5 divide, roll into bases, top with sauce, cheese and toppings, then bake in the airfryer at 200°c for 11 minutes until crisp and golden.

recipes.title: Naan Dough
recipes.search: naan dough naan dough chef magic (knead) → airfryer (bake) 220°c — knead 5 min + rest 1 hr + bake 6 min — makes 6 naans ingredients 2.5 cups all-purpose flour 1 tsp instant yeast 1 tsp sugar 3/4 cup warm milk (105–110°f / 40–43°c) 1/4 cup plain yogurt 2 tbsp oil, plus extra for greasing 1/2 tsp salt melted butter and chopped coriander, to finish method 1 in chef magic, dissolve yeast and sugar in the warm milk heated to 105–110°f (40–43°c) — warm to the touch, not hot; anything above 120°f (49°c) will kill the yeast; let sit 5–10 minutes until frothy. 2 add the flour, yogurt, oil and salt to the jar with the yeast mixture; select knead (speed 2–3, no heat) until a smooth, soft dough forms. 3 lightly grease the dough, cover, and let it rise for about 1 hour, until doubled. 4 divide into 6 portions and roll each into a teardrop or oval shape. 5 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 220°c for 4 minutes before adding the food to the basket. 6 air-fry the naans in batches at 220°c for 5–6 minutes, until puffed and lightly charred in spots. 7 brush with melted butter and scatter over coriander while hot. tip: a light brush of water on top of the shaped naan just before air-frying helps sesame or nigella seeds stick if you'd like to add them.

recipes.title: Basic White Bread Dough
recipes.search: basic white bread dough basic white bread dough chef magic (knead) → airfryer (bake) 180°c — knead 6 min + rise 1.5 hr + bake 25 min — makes 1 small loaf ingredients 3 cups all-purpose flour 2 tsp instant yeast 1.5 tbsp sugar 1 cup warm water (105–110°f / 40–43°c) 2 tbsp oil or melted butter 1 tsp salt method 1 in chef magic, dissolve yeast and sugar in the warm water heated to 105–110°f (40–43°c) — warm to the touch, not hot; anything above 120°f (49°c) will kill the yeast; let sit 5–10 minutes until frothy. 2 add the flour, oil and salt to the jar with the yeast mixture; select knead (speed 2–3, no heat) for 6 minutes until a smooth, elastic dough forms. 3 lightly grease the dough, cover, and let it rise for about 1 hour, until doubled. 4 punch down the dough, shape into a loaf, and place in a greased oven-safe pan that fits the airfryer basket. cover and let rise for another 30 minutes. 5 preheat: preheat the airfryer to 180°c for 4 minutes before adding the food to the basket. 6 bake at 180°c for 22–25 minutes, until golden and the loaf sounds hollow when tapped on the base. 7 cool on a rack for at least 20 minutes before slicing. tip: tent the loaf loosely with foil after the first 15 minutes if the top is browning faster than the inside is cooking through.

recipes.title: Fresh Pasta Dough
recipes.search: fresh pasta dough fresh pasta dough chef magic – knead 6 min + rest 30 min — makes ~400g ingredients 2 cups all-purpose flour (or "00" flour), plus extra for dusting 3 large eggs 1 tbsp olive oil 1/2 tsp salt method 1 add the flour, eggs, olive oil and salt to the jar. 2 select knead (speed 2–3, no heat) and mix until a shaggy dough forms, then continue kneading for 5–6 minutes until smooth and elastic. 3 wrap the dough in cling film and rest at room temperature for 30 minutes. 4 divide into portions and roll out thinly (by hand or pasta machine), dusting with flour as needed, then cut into your desired pasta shape. 5 cook in boiling salted water for 2–3 minutes for fresh pasta, until al dente. tip: resting the dough is essential — skipping this step makes the pasta tough and hard to roll thin, since the gluten needs time to relax.

recipes.title: Shortcrust Pastry (Pie Crust)
recipes.search: shortcrust pastry (pie crust) shortcrust pastry (pie crust) chef magic – mix 3 min + chill 30 min — makes 1 pie base ingredients 1.5 cups all-purpose flour 1/2 tsp salt 1/2 tsp sugar (omit for savoury pies) 115g cold butter, cubed 3–4 tbsp ice-cold water method 1 add the flour, salt and sugar to the jar; pulse briefly on whisk/blend (speed 2) to combine. 2 add the cold butter cubes; pulse in short bursts on whisk/blend (speed 2–3) until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs. 3 add the ice-cold water, 1 tablespoon at a time, pulsing briefly after each addition, until the dough just comes together. 4 turn out, shape into a flat disc, wrap in cling film, and chill for at least 30 minutes before rolling. 5 roll out on a floured surface and use to line a pie or tart tin as required by your recipe. tip: keep everything cold — the butter, the water, even the bowl — for a flaky, tender crust instead of a tough one.

recipes.title: Quick Puff Pastry (Rough Puff)
recipes.search: quick puff pastry (rough puff) quick puff pastry (rough puff) chef magic – mix 3 min + fold & chill 45 min — makes ~400g ingredients 1.5 cups all-purpose flour 1/2 tsp salt 170g cold butter, cubed 1/2 cup ice-cold water 1 tsp lemon juice method 1 add the flour and salt to the jar; pulse briefly on whisk/blend (speed 2) to combine. 2 add the cold butter cubes; pulse briefly, just 2–3 times, so large pea-sized chunks of butter remain visible — do not overmix. 3 mix the ice-cold water with the lemon juice, then add to the jar; pulse just until the dough comes together shaggily. 4 turn out onto a floured surface, shape into a rough rectangle, and roll out. fold into thirds like a letter, then rotate 90 degrees. 5 repeat the roll-fold-rotate process 2 more times, chilling for 15 minutes between folds if the butter softens too much. 6 wrap and chill for at least 30 minutes before rolling out for use. tip: visible chunks of cold butter are exactly what you want — they're what create the flaky layers as the pastry bakes.

recipes.title: Pizza Dough
recipes.search: pizza dough pizza dough chef magic – knead 5 min + rise 1 hr — makes 2 pizza bases ingredients 2.5 cups all-purpose flour, plus extra for dusting 1 tsp instant yeast 1 tsp sugar 1 cup warm water (105–110°f / 40–43°c) 2 tbsp olive oil 1 tsp salt method 1 in chef magic, dissolve yeast and sugar in the warm water heated to 105–110°f (40–43°c) — warm to the touch, not hot; anything above 120°f (49°c) will kill the yeast; let sit 5–10 minutes until frothy. 2 add the flour, olive oil and salt to the jar with the yeast mixture; select knead (speed 2–3, no heat) for 5 minutes until a smooth, elastic dough forms. 3 lightly oil the dough, cover, and let it rise for about 1 hour, until doubled. 4 punch down and divide into 2 portions. roll or stretch each into a base, ready for sauce, cheese and toppings of your choice. 5 use immediately, or wrap and refrigerate for up to 2 days — bring to room temperature before shaping. tip: for an even better base, let the shaped dough rest for 10 minutes before adding toppings — it relaxes the gluten and stops the base from shrinking back as you stretch it.
